STOREBRAND ASA: Resultater for tredje kvartal 2026
body:
Rekordsterkt driftsresultat, drevet av god utvikling i forsikringsvirksomheten
 - Konsernresultat [1] på 1 517 millioner i kvartalet og 4 669 millioner hittil
i år.
 - Driftsresultat på 1 162 millioner, opp 7 prosent sammenlignet med Q3 2025.
 - Forsikringsresultat på 895 millioner, combined ratio på 87 prosent.
 - Egenkapitalavkastning på 15 prosent de siste 12 månedene.
 - Oppkjøp av Knif Trygghet Forsikring gjennomført 16. oktober.
"Storebrand leverer et rekordsterkt driftsresultat i kvartalet, med fortsatt god
underliggende vekst i både spare- og forsikringsvirksomheten. Jeg er godt
fornøyd med veksten i driftsresultatet. Dette gjør at vi er veldig godt i rute
til å levere på 2028-målene om 7 milliarder kroner i konsernresultat og 17
prosent egenkapitalavkastning," sier konsernsjef Odd Arild Grefstad.
"Jeg er særlig fornøyd med at flere store bedrifter valgte Storebrand som
pensjonsleverandør i kvartalet, samtidig som stadig flere personkunder velger
oss som forsikringsleverandør. Vi tar markedsandeler innen forsikring og styrker
posisjonen vår med oppkjøpet av Knif Trygghet Forsikring, som ble gjennomført
16. oktober," sier Grefstad.
"Samfunnet har behov for forebyggende tjenester, og det er derfor ekstra
gledelig at VEL-konseptet vårt nå kan vise til målbare resultater. Hittil i år
har VEL redusert uførekostnadene med rundt 160 millioner kroner, en gevinst som
deles mellom kundene og Storebrand. Vi var tidlig ute og er nå godt posisjonert
med bransjens beste konsept og et bredt leverandørnettverk. At vi kan hjelpe
mennesker tilbake i arbeidslivet, gir mange positive effekter, for
enkeltmennesker, for bedriftene og for samfunnet," sier Grefstad.
"Storebrands strategi er å vokse innen kapitallette produkter og frigjøre
kapital fra den garanterte pensjonsvirksomheten. En sterk balanse kombinert med
økt inntjening gir rom til å både investere i vekst og øke kapitalutdelingen til
aksjonærene. Styret tar sikte på å foreslå et utbytte for 2026 på om lag 6
kroner per aksje og et tilbakekjøpsprogram på 2 milliarder kroner for 2027, opp
fra tidligere kommuniserte 1,5 milliarder, med forbehold om markedsforhold og
nødvendige godkjenninger," sier Grefstad.
Fortsatt resultatvekst og kostnadskontroll på tvers av virksomheten
Fee- og administrasjonsinntekter var 2 139 millioner kroner (2 124 millioner) i
kvartalet. Økt forvaltningskapital ga høyere inntekter. Dette ble delvis
motvirket av lavere prestasjonsbaserte inntekter i kapitalforvaltning,
valutaeffekter og reduserte netto renteinntekter fra banken.
Driftskostnadene var 1 872 millioner kroner i kvartalet, opp fra 1 730 millioner
kroner i tredje kvartal året før. Forsikringssegmentet sto for en stor del av
økningen, med høyere distribusjonskostnader og pågående driftsinvesteringer i
takt med sterk vekst. Innen sparesegmentet er kostnadsveksten under 2 prosent,
med 5 prosent nedgang i kostnadene i kapitalforvaltning. Så langt i år er
kostnadene på konsernnivå opp 5 prosent, i tråd med guidingen.
Storebrand oppnådde et driftsresultat på 1 162 millioner kroner (1 091
millioner) i tredje kvartal, opp 7 prosent fra året før. Dette er et
rekordsterkt driftsresultat, med særlig bidrag fra veksten og
lønnsomhetsforbedringene i forsikring. Innen innskuddspensjon og
kapitalforvaltning økte driftsresultatene med henholdsvis 14 og 11 prosent.
Finansresultatet utgjorde 355 millioner kroner (495 millioner) i kvartalet.
Nedgangen skyldes i hovedsak lavere bidrag fra selskapsporteføljene og
overskuddsdelingen som følge av høyere renter i kvartalet. Høyere renter er
positivt for fremtidig resultatutvikling.
Resultatet etter skatt ble 996 millioner kroner (1 189 millioner), påvirket av
en ekstraordinært høy effektiv skattesats i kvartalet. Dette skyldes at den
norske kronen styrket seg om lag 6 prosent mot den svenske kronen i kvartalet.
Sikringsinstrumenter bidro til at den effektive skattesatsen i kvartalet endte
på 32 prosent. Den forventede normaliserte skattesatsen er 19-22 prosent.
Forsikringssegmentet fortsetter med sterk vekst
Forsikringssegmentet hadde nok et sterkt kvartal, med 28 prosent vekst i
forsikringsresultatet fra året før. Veksten var primært drevet av økte
markedsandeler og lav skadeprosent i personmarkedet. Storebrands markedsandel
innen skadeforsikring i personmarkedet økte til 8,3 prosent, fra 7,6 prosent
året før [2]. Bedriftsmarkedet viste god vekst og stabil lønnsomhet i kvartalet.
Samlet combined ratio for forsikringssegmentet endte på 87 prosent, en
forbedring på 2 prosentpoeng fra tredje kvartal 2025. Premiebestanden økte med
10 prosent over samme periode, til 11,3 milliarder.
Robust balanse og kapitalposisjon
Storebrand opprettholder en robust solvensgrad på 200 prosent, uendret fra
forrige kvartal. Fortsatt sterk resultatgenerering ble motvirket av
igangsettelsen av andre transje av tilbakekjøpsprogrammet for 2026. Endringene i
Solvens II-regelverket og i reguleringen av garanterte pensjonsprodukter ventes
samlet å styrke solvensgraden med mer enn 10 prosentpoeng fra første kvartal
2027.
Nøkkeltall i kvartalet (Q3 2025 i parentes)

 - Egenkapital: 33 223 millioner kroner (32 496 millioner)

 - Egenkapitalavkastning (ROE), siste 12 måneder: 15 prosent (15 prosent)

title: STOREBRAND ASA: Results for the third quarter 2026
body:
Record-strong operating profit, driven by positive development in the insurance
business
 - Group profit [1] of NOK 1,517 million in the quarter and NOK 4,669 million
year to date.
 - Operating profit of NOK 1,162 million, up 7 percent year-on-year.
 - Insurance result of NOK 895 million, combined ratio of 87 percent.
 - Return on Equity of 15 percent over the last twelve months.
 - Acquisition of Knif Trygghet Forsikring completed on 16 October.
"Storebrand delivers record-strong operating profit in the quarter, with still
solid underlying growth in the savings and insurance segments. I am pleased with
the improved operating profit. This means we are well on track to deliver on the
2028 targets of NOK 7 billion in group profit and 17 percent return on equity,"
says CEO Odd Arild Grefstad.
"I am particularly pleased that several large companies chose Storebrand as
their pension provider in the quarter, while a growing number of retail
customers chose us as their insurance provider. We are taking market shares in
insurance and further strengthening our position with the acquisition of Knif
Trygghet Forsikring, completed on 16 October," says Grefstad.
"Society needs preventive services. I am therefore very glad to see our VEL
concept now delivering concrete results. So far this year VEL has reduced
disability claims costs by around NOK 160 million, split between Storebrand and
our customers. We were an early mover and are now well positioned with the
industry's leading concept and a broad network of providers. Helping people back
into work has numerous benefits, for individuals, for businesses and for
society," says Grefstad.
"Storebrand's strategy is to grow in capital-light products and release capital
from the guaranteed pension business. A strong balance sheet combined with
higher earnings give room to both invest in growth and increase capital
distribution to shareholders. The Board intends to propose a dividend of around
NOK 6 per share for 2026 and a share buyback programme of NOK 2 billion for
2027, up from the previously communicated NOK 1.5 billion, subject to market
conditions and necessary approvals," says Grefstad.
Continued earnings growth and cost control across the group
Fee and administration income amounted to NOK 2,139 million (2,124 million) in
the quarter. Growth in assets under management supported higher income. This was
partly offset by lower performance-based income in asset management, currency
effects and lower net interest income in the bank.
Group operational costs amounted to NOK 1,872m in the quarter, up from NOK
1,730m in third quarter last year. The insurance segment accounted for a large
portion of the increase, with higher distribution costs and ongoing investments
in operations to support the strong growth. In the savings segment, cost growth
was below 2 percent, with a 5 percent cost reduction in asset management. Costs
at group level are up 5 percent year to date, in line with guidance.
Storebrand achieved an operating profit of NOK 1,162 million (1,091 million) in
the third quarter, up 7 percent year-on-year. This is a record-strong operating
profit, with a meaningful contribution from the growth and profitability
improvements in insurance. Within Unit Linked and Asset Management, operating
profit increased by 14 and 11 percent, respectively.
The financial result amounted to NOK 355 million (495 million) in the quarter.
The reduction mainly reflects lower contribution from company portfolios and
profit sharing due to rising interest rates in the quarter. Higher interest
rates are supportive for the result development going forward.
The profit after tax was NOK 996 million (1,189 million), affected by an
unusually high effective tax rate in the quarter. This was due to the NOK
appreciating approximately 6 percent against the SEK during the quarter. Hedging
instruments contributed to an effective tax rate of 32 percent. The estimated
normalised tax rate is 19-22 percent.
Strong growth in the insurance segment continued
The insurance segment delivered another strong quarter, with the insurance
result up 28 percent year-on-year. The growth was primarily driven by market
share gains and a low claims ratio in the retail market. Storebrand's market
share within retail P&C insurance increased to 8.3 percent, from 7.6 percent the
year before [2]. The corporate market demonstrated healthy growth and stable
profitability in the quarter.
The overall combined ratio for the insurance segment ended at 87 percent, a 2
percentage point improvement year-on-year. Portfolio premiums increased by 10
percent over the same period, to NOK 11.3 billion.
Robust balance sheet and capital position
Storebrand maintains a robust solvency ratio of 200 percent, unchanged from the
previous quarter. Continued strong result generation was offset by the
initiation of the second tranche of the share buyback programme for 2026. The
amendments to the Solvency II framework and to the regulation of guaranteed
pension products are expected to strengthen the solvency ratio by more than 10
percentage points from the first quarter of 2027.
Key figures in the quarter (Q3 2025 in brackets)
 - Earnings per share (EPS), adjusted for amortisation: NOK 2.54 (NOK 3.08)
 - Equity: NOK 33,223 million (NOK 32,496 million)
 - Assets under management (AuM): NOK 1,633 billion (NOK 1,561 billion)
 - Return on equity (ROE), trailing twelve months: 15 percent (15 percent)
 - Solvency ratio: 200 percent (195 percent)

title: Vår Energi reports strong financial results and increased shareholder returns, whilst continuing to build long-term value
body:
Sandnes, Norway, 21 October 2026: Vår Energi ASA (OSE: VAR, "Vår Energi")
reports strong financial results in the third quarter 2026 and announces
increased shareholder returns, whilst continuing to build long-term value.
Higher production expected in the fourth quarter
 - Solid performance on operated assets with 91% production efficiency YTD
 - Main turnarounds completed in the second and third quarters
 - Higher production expected in the fourth quarter with new projects and wells
onstream
Strong financial position
 - Significant CFFO post tax of USD 1.5 billion in the quarter
 - Successful issuance of USD 2.5 billion senior notes
 - Record high available liquidity of USD 7.5 billion
 - Reduced net debt with leverage at 0.3x
 - Well-positioned to capture upside from higher commodity prices
Unlocking long-term value
 - BlueNord combination progressing towards completion around year-end
 - DNO swap and Pandion acquisition completed in the quarter
 - King Development start-up, adding high-value barrels
 - High Impact Exploration Collaboration established with Equinor and Aker BP
Increased dividend with extraordinary component
 - Increased third quarter dividend and fourth quarter dividend guidance of USD
400 million[1]
 - Long term dividend policy of 25-30% of CFFO after tax over the cycles
"We are pleased to report strong financial results in the third quarter of 2026,
which is supported by high realised oil and gas prices.
With strong cash flow from operations of USD 1.5 billion post tax in the
quarter, materially reduced net debt over the year to USD 3.1 billion and record
high available liquidity of USD 7.5 billion, the Company continues to build
resilience and flexibility.
With the BlueNord combination expected to complete around year end, we are
building the largest independent producer of oil and gas in Europe, with an
increased long term production target of around 450 kboepd.
We continue to strengthen our portfolio and long-term value creation on the
Norwegian Continental Shelf. The Pandion acquisition and DNO swap completed
during the quarter, while we are progressing a portfolio of around 50 new
projects. We are further improving
performance and our outlook by increasing oil and gas recovery, accelerating new
projects and delivering exploration success. Combining technology, strong
partnerships and integrated ways of working through our project factory approach
enables us to realise more value from our resource base, faster and for longer.
Underpinned by continued high prices and strong financial performance, the
Company is increasing shareholder distributions with an extraordinary component.
The Company will distribute USD 400 million for the third quarter of 2026 and is
also guiding USD 400 million for the fourth quarter of 2026[1]. Which means for
the full year we will pay USD 1.45 billion compared to USD 1.2 billion for
2025."
Nick Walker, the CEO of Vår Energi
Q3 2026 webcast
Vår Energi will release its quarterly results on 21 October at 07:00 CEST. A
webcast followed by Q&A will be held at 10:00 CEST, hosted by CEO Nick Walker
and CFO Carlo Santopadre. You can follow the webcast with supporting slides,
available on: https://events.streamhub.no/vaar-energi/quarterly
-reports/nJXQMU6edVK9lVctmW8a
 1. Q3 dividend based on 31.05.26 audited interim balance sheet, and Q4 dividend
subject to 30.09.26 audited interim balance sheet with sufficient free equity
and general meeting approval of dividend. The USD 400 million for the Q3 and Q4
dividend is attributable to the shareholders of the combined company pending
closing of the BlueNord transaction. Completion of the combination is subject to
customary conditions, including partner and authority approvals. Should the
transaction complete after the record date for the Q3 dividend, the cash
consideration payable to BlueNord shareholders will be adjusted to compensate
for the value of the Q3 dividend and any potential further distribution prior to
closing.

title: Solide resultater på tvers av virksomheten i Norden
body:
DNB leverte et resultat etter skatt på 9,8 milliarder kroner i tredje kvartal
2026, som er en nedgang på 839 millioner, eller 7,9 prosent, sammenliknet med
tilsvarende periode i fjor.
- Norsk økonomi er robust. De aller fleste har jobb og en trygg økonomi. Folk
fortsetter å spare og investere, mens bedriftene investerer og utvikler
virksomhetene sine. Det gir et godt utgangspunkt for videre vekst, sier
konsernsjef i DNB Kjerstin Braathen.
- Samtidig ser vi god aktivitet i hele Norden, med særlig sterk vekst i Sverige.
Med DNB Carnegie har vi styrket bredden og den nordiske posisjonen vår, og kan i
enda større grad hjelpe kundene med å realisere sine ambisjoner gjennom
rådgivning og finansiering, sier Braathen.
Flere kunder velger DNB til sparing og investering
DNBs kapitalforvaltning leverte rekordresultater i kvartalet, drevet av sterk
kundevekst og høy kapitalinngang på tvers av virksomheten. Forvaltningskapitalen
i fondsløsningene nådde 1 849 milliarder kroner, opp 67,6 milliarder kroner fra
forrige kvartal, mens nettotegning i fond var rekordhøye 54,5 milliarder
kroner.
- Vi ser en sterk utvikling innenfor sparing og investering, med både flere
kunder og økt sparing. At snittbeholdningen per fondskunde har passert 500 000
kroner og doblet seg på fem år, viser at stadig flere velger fond som en viktig
del av sin langsiktige sparing, sier Braathen.
Årlig fondssparing, gjennom faste spareavtaler, har gått opp 14 prosent så langt
i år, til 12,6 milliarder kroner.
Rekordkvartal for DNB Carnegie Investment Banking
I DNB Carnegie var kundeinntektene sterke i tredje kvartal, med god utvikling på
tvers av regioner og forretningsområder. Inntektene økte med 25 prosent til 2,8
milliarder kroner.
- Integrasjonen av Carnegie går etter planen og gir resultater. Kundene velger
oss til stadig større og mer komplekse transaksjoner, og det bekrefter at vi har
etablert en ledende nordisk plattform med betydelig attraktivitet i markedet,
sier Braathen.
Investment Banking leverte sitt sterkeste tredje kvartal noensinne, drevet av
høy aktivitet og større mandater innen fusjoner og oppkjøp, lån og obligasjoner.
Inntektene fra investeringsbankvirksomheten nådde 1,1 milliarder kroner, en
økning på 44 prosent sammenliknet med tredje kvartal i fjor. Hittil i år er
inntektene fra investeringsbankvirksomheten 3,1 milliarder kroner, opp 30
prosent sammenliknet med samme periode i fjor.
Bedre kundeopplevelser og økt bruk av KI
Utviklingen i personkundemarkedet var positiv gjennom kvartalet, med økt
kundetilfredshet og vekst i både utlån og innskudd sammenliknet med tredje
kvartal i fjor. Utlånsvolumet økte med 1,3 prosent til 989 milliarder kroner,
mens innskuddene økte med 3,8 prosent til 653 milliarder kroner.
- Vi vokser i et marked med sterk konkurranse, samtidig som kundetilfredsheten
går opp. Det er særlig motiverende å se hvordan vi kan bruke KI helt konkret til
å gjøre kundeopplevelsen bedre og gi rådgiverne våre mer tid sammen med kundene,
sier Braathen.
Alle samtaler til kundesenteret går nå gjennom en ny taleportal, hvor 92 prosent
kommer til en rådgiver med riktig kompetanse på første forsøk. Kunderådgiverne
bruker også KI-assistert loggføring, slik at de kan bruke mer av tiden på selve
kundesamtalen.

title: Solid results across operations in the Nordics
body:
DNB delivered profits after tax of NOK 9.8 billion in the third quarter of 2026,
which is a decrease of NOK 839 million, or 7.9 per cent, compared with the
corresponding period last year.
"The Norwegian economy is robust. The vast majority of the population have a job
and secure personal finances. People are continuing to save and invest, while
companies are investing and developing their business operations. This provides
a good starting point for further growth," says CEO of DNB Kjerstin Braathen.
"At the same time, we are seeing good activity throughout the Nordic region,
with particularly strong growth in Sweden. With DNB Carnegie, we have
strengthened the scope of our operations and our Nordic position, and we can to
an even greater extent help customers realise their ambitions through advisory
services and financing," says Braathen.
More customers are choosing DNB for saving and investments
DNB delivered record results in asset management in the quarter, driven by
strong customer growth and high capital inflows across business operations.
Assets under management in DNB's mutual fund solutions reached NOK 1,849
billion, up NOK 67.6 billion from the previous quarter, while there was an all
-time high net flow to mutual funds of NOK 54.5 billion.
"We are seeing a strong development in savings and investments, with both more
customers and increased saving. The fact that the average holding per mutual
fund customer has exceeded NOK 500,000 and has doubled in five years shows that
more and more people are choosing mutual funds as an important part of their
long-term saving," says Braathen.
Annual saving in mutual funds, through fixed savings schemes, has increased by
14 per cent so far this year, to NOK 12.6 billion.
Record quarter for DNB Carnegie Investment Banking
At DNB Carnegie, customer income was strong in the third quarter, with good
development across regions and business areas. Income increased by 25 per cent,
to NOK 2.8 billion.
"The integration of Carnegie is going to plan and yielding results. Customers
are choosing us for increasingly large and more complex transactions, and this
confirms that we have established a leading Nordic platform with significant
standing in the market," says Braathen.
Investment Banking delivered its strongest third quarter ever, driven by a high
level of activity and larger mandates in the areas of mergers and acquisitions,
loans and bonds. Income from investment banking activities reached NOK 1.1
billion, an increase of 44 per cent compared with the third quarter of last
year. So far this year, income from investment banking activities is NOK 3.1
billion, up 30 per cent compared with the same period last year.
Better customer experiences and increased use of AI
Developments in the personal customer market were positive throughout the
quarter, with higher customer satisfaction and growth in both loans and deposits
compared with the third quarter of last year. Lending volumes increased by 1.3
per cent, to NOK 989 billion, while deposits were up 3.8 per cent, to NOK 653
billion.
"We are growing in a highly competitive market, while at the same time customer
satisfaction is rising. It is particularly motivating to see how we can use AI
in concrete terms to improve the customer experience and give our advisers more
time with customers," says Braathen.
All calls to the customer service centre now go through a new digital voice
portal, with 92 per cent of calls reaching an adviser with the right expertise
on the first attempt. The customer advisers also use AI-assisted logging, so
they can spend more of their time on the actual conversation with the
customer.

corresponding quarter of 2025 in parentheses):

title: DNB Bank ASA igangsetter tilbakekjøp av inntil 0,75 prosent av selskapets egne aksjer
category: ACQUISITION OR DISPOSAL OF AN ISSUER'S OWN SHARES
body:
DNB Bank ASA har besluttet å igangsette et nytt program for tilbakekjøp av
inntil 0,75 prosent av selskapets egne aksjer, som tilsvarer 10?804 986 aksjer.
Tilbakekjøpsprogrammet er vedtatt med grunnlag i en fullmakt gitt av siste
ordinære generalforsamling, som ble avholdt 21. april 2026. Finanstilsynet har
godkjent tilbakekjøpsprogrammet, under den forutsetning at de samlede
tilbakekjøpene ikke reduserer egenkapitalen med mer enn 3 790 millioner kroner.
Tilbakekjøpsprogrammet har til formål å optimalisere selskapets kapitalstruktur
gjennom å redusere den rene kjernekapitaldekningen med omtrent 0,3
prosentpoeng.
Av den totale rammen for tilbakekjøp vil inntil 0,495 prosent av selskapets egne
aksjer, tilsvarende 7?131 291 aksjer, bli kjøpt på handelsplasser til en pris på
mellom 10 og 400 kroner per aksje. Tilbakekjøpene skal være avsluttet innen 18.
desember 2026. DNB Carnegie har fått i oppdrag å kjøpe tilbake aksjene på vegne
av selskapet og vil beslutte når kjøpene skal gjennomføres, uavhengig av
selskapet. De tilbakekjøpte aksjene vil bli foreslått slettet på neste ordinære
generalforsamling.
På den samme generalforsamlingen vil de resterende 0,255 prosentene av aksjene -
inntil 3?673?695 aksjer - bli foreslått innløst fra den norske stat ved Nærings-
og fiskeridepartementet ("NFD"), slik at NFDs eierandel på 34 prosent forblir
uendret. Innløsningen vil bli gjort til en pris tilsvarende gjennomsnittsprisen
på aksjene som kjøpes tilbake på handelsplasser, tillagt en rentekompensasjon.
Tilbakekjøpsprogrammet vil bli gjennomført i samsvar med
markedsmisbruksforordningen og forordningen om tilbakekjøpsprogrammer og
stabiliseringstiltak.
Selskapet eier allerede 19?016 776 egne aksjer, som ble kjøpt tilbake tidligere
i 2026.

title: DNB Bank ASA initiates share buy-back programme of up to 0.75 per cent of its own shares
category: ACQUISITION OR DISPOSAL OF AN ISSUER'S OWN SHARES
body:
DNB Bank ASA has decided to initiate a new share buy-back programme comprising
up to 0.75 per cent of the company's own shares, which represents a total of
10,804,986 shares. The buy-back programme was adopted based on an authorisation
given by the Annual General Meeting held on 21 April?2026. The Financial
Supervisory Authority of Norway has approved the buy-back programme, on the
condition that the total buy-backs do not reduce the company's own funds by more
than NOK 3,790 million.
The purpose of the buy-back programme is to optimise the company's capital
structure, by reducing the common equity tier 1 (CET1) ratio by approximately
0.3 percentage points.
Up to 0.495 per cent of the company's own shares, which equals 7,131,291 shares,
will be bought back on trading venues, at a price of between NOK 10 and NOK 400
per share. The buy-backs will, at the latest, end on 18 December 2026. DNB
Carnegie will manage the buy-backs on behalf of the company and decide the
timing of the purchases independently of the company. The shares that are
purchased will be proposed cancelled at the next Annual General Meeting.
The remaining 0.255 per cent of the shares - up to 3,673,695 shares - will at
the same Annual General Meeting be proposed redeemed from the Norwegian
Government, represented by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries
("NFD"), so that NFD's ownership interest of 34 per cent remains unchanged.
NFD's shares will be redeemed at a price equal to the average price of the
shares bought back on trading venues, with the addition of an interest
compensation.
The buy-back programme will be carried out in accordance with the Market Abuse
Regulation and the regulation regarding buy-back programmes and stabilisation
measures.
The company currently owns 19,016,776 own shares, which were repurchased earlier
in 2026.

title: TOMRA: Appointed preferred supplier to leading retail chain in UK
Scatec revises full-year 2026 power production EBITDA estimate
body:
Oslo, 21 October 2026: Scatec has revised its full-year 2026 power production
EBITDA estimate down by NOK 300 million to NOK 3,300 to 3,600 million.
The revision reflects several adverse developments:
* Russia has intensified its attacks on energy infrastructure in Ukraine. This
 is causing disruptions to operations of Scatec's power plants in the country
 and delays in repair works for the power plant that sustained a direct
 attack in 2025. The prolonged war is also negatively impacting the country
 risk assessment and longer-term power price outlook.
* In the Philippines, the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) announced on 12
 October that the reserves market for ancillary services has been suspended.
 The market operator has been asked to propose a redesigned market structure
 to limit elevated prices within six months, and in the meantime seek to
 enter longer term contracts to meet demand for ancillary services.
* In South Africa, commercial operation of the Mogobe battery energy storage
 system is delayed due to delayed connection work by state-owned utility
 Eskom.
* In Pakistan, the true-up process for the electricity tariff, previously
 expected to be resolved during 2026, is likely to be delayed.
* Since last reporting, exchange rates for key operating currencies of Scatec
 have continued to weaken relative to NOK which negatively impacts the 2026
 EBITDA estimate.
Scatec continues to assess the financial implications of these developments
and will provide further updates at the third quarter results presentation on
30 October 2026.

title: NOD: Third quarter results 2026
body:
(Oslo, Norway - October 22, 2026) Nordic Semiconductor ASA reports revenue of USD 235 million for the third quarter 2026, an increase of 32% from the third quarter 2025. Gross margin improved to 53% from 52% in the same quarter last year. Reported EBITDA more than doubled to USD 39 million from USD 16 million in the third quarter last year, with adjusted EBITDA increasing to USD 40 million from USD 18 million in the same period last year. The adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 10% in the third quarter 2025.
This represents another record quarterly revenue level for Nordic Semiconductor. Short-range revenue increased 30% to USD 216 million, with continued solid demand from both key customers and the broad market in all main end-user markets, whereas Long-range revenue increased by 70% to USD 17 million with increasing sales from a broader product portfolio and continuing growth in nRF Cloud Services revenue. Other revenue increased 18% year-on-year to USD 3 million.
-Customer demand continued to grow in the third quarter, and we remain focused on delivering our plan across financial, operational and strategic priorities. We are continuously launching new products that strengthen our competitive position and expand our addressable market, and we see rapid adoption of the AI-assisted development tools we have launched to help our customers become even more productive, says CEO Vegard Wollan in Nordic Semiconductor.
-While our revenue growth has been strongest in the broad market over the past year, we also see a strong pipeline with key customers working towards introducing more intelligent end-user devices in the time to come. We have a very strong offering across compute performance, memory capabilities, power usage and compact size, and combined with leading edge AI hardware, software and tools this makes us well-positioned to benefit from the megatrend of universal AI adoption, adds Wollan.
Revenue for the first nine months 2026 amounted to USD 646 million, up 30% compared to the first nine months 2025. Reported EBITDA for the first nine months increased to USD 93 million from USD 51 million in the same period last year, whereas adjusted EBITDA increased to USD 100 million from USD 54 million in the first nine months 2025.
On a rolling 12 months basis, revenue increased by 26% year-on-year to USD 816 million.
Based on current customer orders and forecasts, Nordic expects revenue for the fourth quarter 2026 of USD 215-235 million. The gross margin is expected to remain above 50% also in the fourth quarter.
The revenue and margin developments continue to support Nordic's long-term financial ambitions presented in 2024; to deliver average annual revenue growth above 20% from 2024 through the end of the decade, maintain a gross margin above 50%, and move towards the target operating model profitability level of 25% EBITDA margin.

title: Kitron: Strong and broad-based growth
body:
(2026-10-22) Kitron today reported strong growth in revenue and operating
profit, along with a record order backlog, reflecting robust demand across
market sectors.
Kitron's revenue for the third quarter was EUR 266.8 million, an increase of 59
per cent from 167.8 million in the same quarter last year. The Defence/Aerospace
market sector continued to show an exceptional increase from last year, but
there was solid progress across other market sectors as well.
Third-quarter operating profit (EBIT) was EUR 25.2 million, compared with 14.6
million in the same quarter last year, an increase of 73 per cent. Profitability
expressed as EBIT margin was 9.5 per cent, compared with 8.7 per cent in the
same quarter last year. This is in line with the strategic target of maintaining
an EBIT margin above 9 per cent.
The order backlog ended at EUR 843.3 million, an increase of 41 per cent
compared with last year, reflecting broad-based demand across market sectors.
Peter Nilsson, Kitron's CEO, comments:
"This was a quarter where the shape of our growth changed. Over the past year,
Defence & Aerospace has led the way. In the third quarter, growth was broader.
Electrification is where the change is clearest. We will enter 2027 on a broader
base than we started 2026 with."
Profit after tax amounted to EUR 17.4 million, compared with 9.1 million in the
same quarter of the previous year. This corresponds to earnings per share of EUR
0.08, up from 0.05 last year.
Outlook
For 2026, Kitron expects revenue of EUR 1050 to 1150 million. Operating profit
(EBIT) is expected to be between EUR 97 and 112 million. This is unchanged from
the lifted outlook published on 24 August.

presented today at 8.30 a.m. CEST by CEO Peter Nilsson and CFO Cathrin Nylander.

title: Kitron: Sterk og bred vekst
body:

samt rekordhøy ordrereserve, noe som reflekterer robust etterspørsel i flere
markedssektorer.
Kitrons driftsinntekter for tredje kvartal var 266,8 millioner euro, en økning

Forsvar/Luftfart fortsatte den eksepsjonelle veksten fra året før, men det var
også solid fremgang i flere andre markedssektorer.

Endringen er tydeligst innen Elektrifisering. Vi går inn i 2027 med en bredere
plattform enn vi hadde ved starten av 2026.
Resultatet etter skatt utgjorde 17,4 millioner euro, sammenlignet med 9,1

title: TGS Announces Q3 2026 Results
body:
OSLO, Norway (22 October 2026) - TGS today reports interim financial results for
Q3 2026.
Financial highlights:
 * Revenues of USD 397 million driven by high contract activity, compared to
 USD 388 million in Q3 2025
 * EBITDA of USD 222 million, including USD 41 million in gain from sale of the
 well data business, compared to USD 242 million in Q3 2025
 * EBIT of USD 86 million, including USD 41 million in gain from sale of the
 well data business, compared to USD 94 million in Q3 2025
 * Cost impacted by operational challenges
 * Robust order inflow1 of USD 357 million resulting in a total order backlog1
 of USD 679 million, a Y/Y increase of 52%
 * Dividend of USD 0.155 per share to be paid in Q4 2026
"The third quarter saw strong contract activity across both the 3D streamer
vessel fleet and the Ocean Bottom Node (OBN) operations, resulting in the
highest contract revenues since the fourth quarter of 2024. Although a higher
activity level led to year-over-year growth in revenue, margins were negatively
impacted by a combination of higher costs, driven by operational challenges, and
low contract pricing. Going forward we are pleased to see a stronger pipeline of
streamer contract opportunities, with clients competing for available capacity
on several occasions. This development gives us confidence that contract pricing
will improve from 2027. In OBN, tendering activity continues to increase,
reinforcing our expectation of higher activity levels next year.
Our order intake continues to be strong, supported by a healthy mix of new
contract awards and multi-client projects during the quarter, bringing total
backlog to USD 679 million, up 52% from Q3 last year. The streamer fleet is
fully booked for the fourth quarter, and visibility has improved significantly
compared with the same period last year, enabling us to optimize asset
allocation. Given the increased volume of contract work in the pipeline, we have
decided to defer certain multi-client projects. As a result, we now expect
multi-client investments in 2026 to be approximately USD 510 million, compared
with our previous guidance of approximately USD 550 million.

title: Kongsberg Automotive s transformation continues to deliver stronger earnings
body:
Kongsberg, October 22, 2026: Kongsberg Automotive ASA (KA) has released its
results for the third quarter of 2026, reporting increased revenues and
stronger earnings. KA's transformation continues to deliver tangible results,
with improved profitability and capital efficiency. 
Highlights for Q3 2026 (Q3 2025 in brackets):
* Revenue MEUR 185.2 (MEUR 162.9)
* EBIT MEUR 9.0 (MEUR 4.9)
* Net profit: MEUR 6.4 (MEUR 1.6)
* Net cash flow: MEUR 2.2 (MEUR 6.6)
Revenues increased to MEUR 185.2 from MEUR 162.9 in Q3 2025, primarily driven
by stronger sales to commercial vehicle markets in North America. EBIT
increased to MEUR 9.0, corresponding to a margin of 4.8%, compared with MEUR
4.9 and a margin of 3.0% in Q3 last year. The improvement reflects higher
activity levels and stronger operational performance.
Alongside the continued progress in financial and operational performance, KA
remains focused on profitable growth and long-term value creation. During the
quarter, KA secured contracts with estimated lifetime revenues of MEUR 142.0,
consisting of both incremental new business and extensions of existing
contracts. New contracts are being secured on improved commercial and
contractual terms, reflecting KA's focus on the quality and profitability of
new business.
"I am encouraged by the progress we are making. The actions taken over the
past year are increasingly translating into tangible financial results. These
results reflect a broader transformation of Kongsberg Automotive into a more
focused, disciplined and accountable company. We will continue to raise our
ambitions and execute with discipline as we build a more profitable,
capital-efficient, and resilient company capable of creating long-term value
for our shareholders," says Trond Fiskum, President & CEO.
Additionally, on October 21, 2026, the Board of Directors approved a new
Dividend Policy aimed at providing shareholders with competitive and
sustainable returns over time. The Dividend Policy is available on KA's
website.

title: Atea Q3 2026 financial report and presentation
body:
Atea reported strong growth in sales and profitability in the third quarter of
2026, driven by high demand for data center solutions.
Gross sales in Q3 increased by 12.6% to NOK 13.9 billion. All sales growth was
organic. Hardware sales grew by 25.0% and software/cloud sales grew by 3.3%,
while services sales were 1.9% lower than last year.
Currency fluctuations had a negative impact of 7.5% on sales growth, as sales in
foreign currencies were translated to a stronger Norwegian krone compared with
last year. Adjusted for changes in currency rates, organic sales growth in
constant currency was 21.7%.
Net revenue (IFRS) grew by 16.9% to NOK 9.9 billion. Atea's gross margin was
26.0% in Q3 2026, down from 29.8% last year, due primarily to an increased
proportion of hardware in the revenue mix. Operating expenses fell by 0.3% to
NOK 2.2 billion. The average number of full-time employees increased by 63
(0.8%) from last year.
Based on strong sales performance and low growth in operating costs, EBIT in Q3
2026 increased by 16.5% to NOK 405 million. Profit before tax increased by 24.1%
to NOK 362 million. Net profit after tax was NOK 279 million, compared with NOK
226 million last year.
Atea CEO Steinar Sønsteby commented: "Atea's strong momentum continued in Q3, as
we gained market share and delivered organic sales growth of 22% in constant
currency. We achieved this growth with almost no increase in staffing,
demonstrating our ability to capture efficiency gains. Demand remains
particularly robust for datacenter equipment, a segment where Atea has a strong
market position. Higher hardware prices are also supporting growth. Looking
ahead, we expect strong financial performance to continue in 2027, driven by
favorable market conditions, further market share gains and continued efficiency
improvements."
The interim report and presentation are available at:
www.atea.com/financial-reports/
A webcast of management's presentation of the financial results is available at:
www.atea.com/financial-reports/2026/webcast-q3-26/

Atea is the leading supplier of IT infrastructure in the Nordic and Baltic

title: Yara reports solid 3Q amid market volatility
body:
Yara reports third quarter 2026 EBITDA excluding special items[1] of USD 675
million compared with USD 804 million in third quarter 2025. Net income for the
quarter was USD 199 million compared with USD 320 million a year earlier.
Third quarter of 2026 highlights:
 - EBITDA excluding special items[1] of 675 MUSD and ROIC[1] of 13.5%
 - European nitrate volume rebound in the quarter - global 2027 season buying
significantly behind previous years
 - Higher gas prices and continued deferred demand weighed on margins and
deliveries for the quarter
 - Strong focus on cost control, improving reliability and accelerating EBITDA
improvements
 - Gulf Coast Ammonia acquisition will increase gas diversification upon
closing[2]
"We delivered a solid third-quarter result despite continued market volatility.
Strong commercial performance helped offset accelerating European gas costs
while plant-specific reliability issues affected production volumes.. Yara's
energy flexibility has been a key strength and will remain even more so, with
the acquisition of Gulf Coast Ammonia significantly reducing our European energy
exposure upon closing. We remain on track to deliver our EBITDA improvement
target, and the increase in return on invested capital reflects stronger
underlying profitability," said Svein Tore Holsether, President and Chief
Executive Officer.
Nitrogen markets had a slow start to the new season as markets took a cautious
approach due to uncertainty around the Middle East conflict. Yara saw buying
activity, particularly in Europe, picking up towards the end of the quarter, and
Yara exits the quarter with a European order book stronger than normal for this
time of year. Market demand for the 2027 season has been slow across all key
nitrogen markets in Q3, with imports and deliveries in Europe, the US and Latin
America lagging last year's levels. As the Chinese export window is closing and
Northern Hemisphere season approaches, a significant share of seasonal
purchasing therefore remains to be done for the first full season with reduced
supply from the Middle East, where also higher crop prices have improved farmer
affordability compared to last season.
Yara actively managed its European production footprint during the quarter in
response to high European gas prices, leveraging the flexibility of its global
production network and supply chain. By optimizing product flows, closely
monitoring margins and adjusting production as market conditions evolved, Yara
continued to supply customers while reducing exposure to elevated energy costs.
"In volatile markets, diversification and flexibility are critical to food
security and industrial resilience. We are strengthening Yara's competitiveness
through disciplined EBITDA improvement measures, strict capital discipline and
by addressing recent reliability setbacks. Our premium portfolio, global
production network and ability to optimize across products, assets and regions
make Yara more resilient, further strengthened by our investment in the US.
Combined, these actions will support higher base returns and sustainable
shareholder value," said Holsether.

title: Yara rapporterer solide Q3-resultater i et volatilt marked
body:
Yara rapporterer EBITDA eksklusive spesielle poster[1] på 675 millioner USD i
tredje kvartal 2026, sammenlignet med 804 millioner USD i tredje kvartal 2025.
Resultat etter skatt var 199 millioner USD, mot 320 millioner USD året før.
Hovedpunkter fra kvartalet:
 - EBITDA eksklusive spesielle poster[1] på 675 millioner USD og ROIC[1] på
13,5%
 - Oppgang i europeiske nitratleveranser gjennom kvartalet - innkjøp til den
globale 2027-sesongen betydelig bak tidligere år
 - Høyere gasspriser og fortsatt utsatt etterspørsel påvirket marginer og
leveranser i kvartalet
 - Sterkt fokus på kostnadskontroll, økt driftsstabilitet og videre EBITDA
-forbedringer
 - Oppkjøpet av Gulf Coast Ammonia vil øke diversifisering av gasseksponeringen
etter transaksjonen er gjennomført[2]
- Vi leverte et solid resultat i tredje kvartal til tross for vedvarende uro i
markedet. Sterk kommersiell fremgang bidro til å motvirke økende europeiske
gasskostnader og driftsutfordringer ved enkelte anlegg. Yaras
energifleksibilitet har vært en viktig styrke, og vil styrkes ytterligere etter
oppkjøpet av Gulf Coast Ammonia er gjennomført, som reduserer eksponeringen mot
europeiske energipriser betydelig. Vi er i rute for å nå våre EBITDA
-forbedringsmål, og høyere avkastning på investert kapital gjenspeiler sterkere
underliggende lønnsomhet, sier Svein Tore Holsether, konsernsjef i Yara.
Usikkerheten rundt situasjonen i Midtøsten førte til avventende kjøpsaktivitet
og en treg start på den nye sesongen i nitrogenmarkedet. Aktiviteten tok seg opp
mot slutten av kvartalet, særlig i Europa, og Yara går ut av kvartalet med en
europeisk ordrebok som er sterkere enn normalt på denne tiden av året. En
betydelig del av innkjøpene for 2027-sesongen gjenstår i de viktigste
nitrogenmarkedene, etter at import og leveranser i Europa, USA og Latin-Amerika
har ligget under fjorårets nivå. Samtidig nærmer det kinesiske eksportvinduet
seg slutten, i den første hele sesongen med redusert forsyning fra Midtøsten.
Høyere avlingspriser har også forbedret bøndenes kjøpekraft sammenlignet med
forrige sesong.
Yara tilpasset den europeiske produksjonen gjennom kvartalet som følge av høye
gasspriser. Gjennom fleksibilitet i det globale produksjons- og
logistikknettverket kunne Yara optimalisere varestrømmene, følge
marginutviklingen tett og tilpasse produksjonen i takt med markedsforholdene. På
den måten kunne selskapet fortsette leveranser til kundene og samtidig redusere
eksponeringen mot høye europeiske energikostnader.
- I volatile markeder er diversifisering og fleksibilitet avgjørende for
matsikkerhet og industriell robusthet. Vi styrker Yaras konkurransekraft gjennom
målrettede tiltak for å forbedre EBITDA, streng kapitaldisiplin og tiltak for å
bedre driftsstabiliteten. Vår portefølje av premium produkter, globale
produksjonsplattform og fleksibilitet på tvers av produkter, anlegg og regioner
gjør Yara mer robust. Dette styrkes ytterligere gjennom investeringen i USA.
Samlet vil disse tiltakene bidra til høyere underliggende avkastning og
verdiskaping for aksjonærene, sier Holsether.

title: TGS Announces Q3 2026 Results - Correction
body:

Everything else unchanged.
OSLO, Norway (22 October 2026) - TGS today reports interim financial results for
Q3 2026.
Financial highlights:
 * Revenues of USD 397 million driven by high contract activity, compared to
 USD 388 million in Q3 2025
 * EBITDA of USD 222 million, including USD 41 million in gain from sale of the
 well data business, compared to USD 242 million in Q3 2025
 * EBIT of USD 86 million, including USD 41 million in gain from sale of the
 well data business, compared to USD 94 million in Q3 2025
 * Cost impacted by operational challenges
 * Robust order inflow1 of USD 357 million resulting in a total order backlog1
 of USD 679 million, a Y/Y increase of 52%
 * Dividend of USD 0.155 per share to be paid in Q4 2026
"The third quarter saw strong contract activity across both the 3D streamer
vessel fleet and the Ocean Bottom Node (OBN) operations, resulting in the
highest contract revenues since the fourth quarter of 2024. Although a higher
activity level led to year-over-year growth in revenue, margins were negatively
impacted by a combination of higher costs, driven by operational challenges, and
low contract pricing. Going forward we are pleased to see a stronger pipeline of
streamer contract opportunities, with clients competing for available capacity
on several occasions. This development gives us confidence that contract pricing
will improve from 2027. In OBN, tendering activity continues to increase,
reinforcing our expectation of higher activity levels next year.
Our order intake continues to be strong, supported by a healthy mix of new
contract awards and multi-client projects during the quarter, bringing total
backlog to USD 679 million, up 52% from Q3 last year. The streamer fleet is
fully booked for the fourth quarter, and visibility has improved significantly
compared with the same period last year, enabling us to optimize asset
allocation. Given the increased volume of contract work in the pipeline, we have
decided to defer certain multi-client projects. As a result, we now expect
multi-client investments in 2026 to be approximately USD 510 million, compared
with our previous guidance of approximately USD 550 million.
Sustained high oil prices have strengthened our customers' cash flows, while a
marked increase in acreage awards has created a growing inventory of areas yet
to be evaluated and explored. Together, these developments are driving demand
for high-quality seismic data and reinforce our confidence in the opportunities

title: DOF Group ASA - Awarded subsea installation contract in Africa
body:
DOF Group ASA ("DOF") is pleased to announce the award of a Significant* subsea
contract in Africa.
The contract will be executed by Skandi Acergy and is scheduled to commence in
early Q1 2027 with an expected duration of approximately 100 days.
DOF shall under this contract deliver project management, engineering, logistics
and offshore execution services for the transportation and installation of
various Subsea Production Systems (SPS) in deep-water field developments.
Project management, engineering and planning activities will be delivered by
DOF's Atlantic region teams in Bergen and Aberdeen, whilst offshore execution
will be carried out during a dedicated offshore campaign in support of the
client's field development objectives.
Mons S. Aase, DOF Group ASA CEO, said:
"We are pleased to secure this award and the trust placed in DOF by a leading
operator. Deep-water SPS installation is a critical phase in the development of
any field and requires careful planning, strong engineering and proven execution
capability. Our priority will be to safeguard the installation, effectively
manage project risks and deliver the work safely, efficiently and on schedule.
We look forward to supporting our client in the successful delivery of this
project."
The award further strengthens DOF's position in the African subsea market and
adds to the company's backlog for 2027.
DOF defines a Significant contract as a contract with a value between USD 15
million and USD 25 million.

title: Danmark annonserer planer om å anskaffe Joint Strike-missiler
Denmark announces plans to acquire JSM missiles
body:
The Kingdom of Denmark has today announced its intention to acquire KONGSBERG's Joint Strike Missile for its fleet of F-35 aircraft.
Denmark is the seventh nation to select the JSM. The scope and value of the contract will be determined by negotiations with the customer. KONGSBERG will update the market after a contract has been signed. 
The JSM is a 5th generation stealth air-to surface missile, which can be carried internally in the F-35A thus ensuring the aircraft's low-signature capabilities.
The JSM has been selected by Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, Norway and the United States.
KONGSBERG (OSE ticker: KOG) is an international technology and defence company that delivers critical products and solutions in defence, security and surveillance on land, underwater and in space. KONGSBERG has approximately 7 800 employees in 20 countries and had a total revenue of NOK 32.8 billion in 2025.

title: Scatec and EBRD establish renewable energy investment platform in Egypt
body:
Oslo/Cairo, 22 October 2026: Scatec ASA ("Scatec"), a leading renewable energy
solutions provider, and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
("EBRD") have signed a share purchase agreement establishing a renewable
energy investment platform for Egypt. The platform will be owned 60% by Scatec
and 40% by EBRD. EBRD has committed up to USD 221 million to the platform, of
which approximately USD 170 million as equity and the remaining as
project-level guarantees.
The platform is designed primarily to accelerate the development and financing
of Scatec's near-term renewable energy portfolio in Egypt. It is expected to
hold 40% equity interest in the Obelisk project, 51% in Shadwan and
approximately 60% equity interest in the Egypt Aluminium phase 1 (Dandara) and
Energy Valley projects, alongside other minority co-investors. Over time, the
platform may also invest in additional opportunities across the broader MENA
region.
"Egypt has become one of Scatec's most important markets, and this platform
reflects both the scale of what we are building there and the quality of the
assets we have developed. Partnering with EBRD brings institutional capital
and a long-term commitment that will accelerate Scatec's growth ambitions
across the region," says Scatec CEO Terje Pilskog.
"This equity investment marks an important step in strengthening Egypt's
energy security. By partnering with Scatec, EBRD is providing long-term
capital as a shareholder, helping expand access to reliable renewable energy.
This will help address one of the country's most pressing development
challenges while reducing reliance on imported fossil fuels," says Harry
Boyd-Carpenter, Managing Director, Sustainable Infrastructure at EBRD.
The platform demonstrates Scatec's strategy of partnering with long-term
institutional investors, scaling renewable energy investments in markets with
strong fundamentals, and enhancing capital efficiency through recycling
capital. By combining Scatec's development, execution and asset management
capabilities with EBRD's regional expertise and financing capacity, the
platform will strengthen project delivery, support Egypt's energy transition
and provide a replicable model for future growth in selected markets across
the region.
The platform is structured through a holding vehicle, in which EBRD will
invest with Scatec. Scatec will remain the lead sponsor, developer, EPC
provider and asset manager across the projects within the platform.
About EBRD
The EBRD is a multilateral bank that promotes the development of the private
sector and entrepreneurial initiative in 40 economies across three continents.
The Bank is owned by 77 countries as well as the EU and the EIB. EBRD
investments are aimed at making the economies in its
regions competitive, inclusive, well
governed, green, resilient and integrated. The EBRD is a leading institutional
investor in Egypt. Since starting operations there in 2012, it has invested
more than 16 billion through 238 projects.
For further information, please contact:

Andreas Austrell, SVP Investor Relations
andreas.austrell@scatec.com

About Scatec
Scatec is a leading renewable energy solutions provider, accelerating access

title: Norsk Hydro: Solide resultater og god drift
body:
Hydros justerte EBITDA var 9.089 millioner kroner i tredje kvartal 2026, en
økning fra 5.996 millioner kroner i samme kvartal i fjor. Høyere all-in
metallpriser og høyere aluminapriser bidro positivt, sammen med bedre inntjening
i Recycling og Extrusions. Resultatet ble delvis utlignet av høyere anode- og
energikostnader i Aluminium Metal, økte energikostnader i Bauxite & Alumina
grunnet forstyrrelser i gassforsyningen, en sterkere norsk krone i forhold til
USD, og tap på forskjeller mellom prisområder i Energy.
 * Alunorte startet opp normal drift etter midlertidige forstyrrelser i
 gassforsyningen
 * Fri kontantstrøm på 1,4 milliarder kroner påvirket av høyere metallpriser og
 tilhørende krav til arbeidskapital og forskuddsbetalinger
 * Første metallproduksjon ved testanlegget HalZero, en viktig milepæl i
 utviklingen av karbonfri teknologi
 * Den kommersielle utviklingen fortsetter for Hydros portefølje av lavkarbon-
 og resirkulert aluminium
 * Nye langsiktige avtaler om kraftkjøp (PPA) er inngått og styrker Hydros
 langsiktige kraftposisjon ytterligere
Hydro hadde høy lønnsomhet i kvartalet, og justert resultat per aksje har økt
fra 1,00 kroner i tredje kvartal 2025 til 2,30 kroner i tredje kvartal 2026. Fri
kontantstrøm var 1,4 milliarder kroner, med en høy justert EBITDA som ble delvis
utlignet av høyere netto driftskapital, i hovedsak drevet av økte metallpriser,
tilhørende krav til arbeidskapital og forskuddsbetalinger. Selv om denne
utviklingen reflekterer dagens markedsforhold, vil det legges betydelig vekt på
kontantstrøm og økt effektivitet i styring av arbeidskapital i tiden framover.
Som følge av dette har Hydro redusert investeringsmålet ved utgangen av året fra
13,5 milliarder kroner til rundt 12,5 milliarder kroner, og økt antatt netto
arbeidskapital fra 30 milliarder kroner til rundt 32 milliarder kroner. Justert
RoaCE over de siste tolv månedene endte på 12,5 prosent.
- Hydros resultater for tredje kvartal reflekterer god drift, som ble forsterket
av gunstige markedsforhold. Rekordhøy produksjon av flytende metall fra de
norske verkene og høye priser i hele kvartalet har gitt solid inntjening og høy
lønnsomhet. God drift gjør at vi kan utnytte mer av oppsiden når
markedsforholdene er gode og ikke minst gjør det oss mer robuste når markedet
snur, sier Hydros konsernsjef, Eivind Kallevik.
I tredje kvartal oppsto det forstyrrelser i forsyningen av naturgass til
Alunorte, noe som førte til en midlertidig reduksjon i produksjonen ved
raffineriet. Basert på ulike tiltak, inkludert gjennom å sikre alternativ
forsyning av LNG, var Hydro i stand til å opprettholde driften og gjenoppta
produksjonen av alumina.
Aluminium Metal dro fordel av høyere all-in metallpriser og solid drift, mens
Recycling og Extrusions hadde bedre inntjening som følge av høye
resirkuleringsmarginer. De norske metallverkene økte produksjonen av flytende
metall til et rekordhøyt nivå, og befester Hydros posisjon som en pålitelig
leverandør av lavkarbonaluminium til europeiske kunder.
Samtidig opplever Hydro fortsatt framgang for lavkarbon- og resirkulerte
produkter, med ledende merkenavn som CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty, General
Motors og Mercedes-Benz, som bruker Hydros løsninger i sitt sortiment.
- Vi ser fortsatt stor etterspørsel etter våre lavkarbon- og resirkulerte
produkter fra noen av verdens ledende forbrukermerker. Når merkenavn som CHANEL
Fragrances and Beauty og Mercedes-Benz velger Hydro, har de tillit til vår
kvalitet, pålitelighet og evne til å hjelpe dem å nå sine ambisjoner. Den
tilliten har kommersiell verdi, og styrker vår tro på de langsiktige mulighetene
for lavkarbon- og resirkulert aluminium, sier Kallevik
Hydro nådde en viktig milepæl i utviklingen av sin HalZero-teknologi med
produksjon av aluminium for første gang, og utprøving av elektrolyseteknologien
utover laboratorieskala. Denne milepælen er et viktig steg på veien i Hydros
langsiktige ambisjon om utslippsfri elektrolyse- og anodeproduksjon. Det
gjenstår ytterligere testing, pilotprøving og teknologiutvikling før eventuell
bruk i industriell skala. Enova har innvilget 82 millioner kroner til
konseptutvikling og planlegging av en industrielt pilotanlegg.
- Dette er en viktig milepæl og et viktig steg på veien i utviklingen av
HalZero. Denne første produksjonen av metall viser at elektrolyseteknologien
fungerer, og åpner for fortsatt utvikling av en banebrytende teknologi som kan
gi utslippsfri produksjon av aluminium i framtiden, sier Kallevik.
I kvartalet begynte Slovalco arbeidet med å starte opp igjen produksjonen av
primæraluminium, etter en avtale om langsiktige rammebetingelser med den
slovakiske regjeringen som ble kunngjort i juli. Produksjonen ble startet sent i
august, og innebærer at kapasitet som ble stengt ned i forbindelse med den
europeiske energikrisen i 2022 nå blir tilbakeført. I den første fasen tas det
sikte på en årlig produksjonskapasitet på 75.000 tonn innen utgangen av februar
2027. Oppstarten reflekterer betydningen av konkurransedyktig kraft,
forutsigbare rammebetingelser og en effektiv industripolitikk som kan
opprettholde og gjenoppbygge industrigrunnlaget i Europa.
Resultater og markedsutvikling i forretningsområdene
Justert EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina gikk ned fra 1.290 millioner kroner til
283 millioner kroner, sammenlignet med tredje kvartal i fjor. Nedgangen skyldtes
hovedsakelig lavere aluminapriser, forstyrrelser i naturgassforsyningen som ga
høyere kostnader knyttet til kjøp av LNG, og ugunstige valutaeffekter i
kursforholdet mellom BRL/USD. Dette ble delvis motvirket av lavere
råvarekostnader og lavere faste kostnader.
Prisene på Platts aluminaindeks (PAX) gikk opp i tredje kvartal 2026, til 370
USD ved utgangen av kvartalet, noe som avvek fra kinesiske aluminapriser, som
gikk ned. Til tross for lavere aluminaproduksjon ved enkelte raffinerier i

title: Norsk Hydro: Solid results and strong performance
body:
Hydro's adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 9,089 million, up
from NOK 5,996 million in the same quarter last year. Higher all-in metal prices
and higher alumina prices contributed positively in the quarter, along with
improved earnings in Recycling and Extrusions. The strong performance was
partially offset by higher anode and energy costs in Aluminium Metal, increased
energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions, a stronger NOK
vs USD, and negative price area differences in Energy.
 * Alunorte resumed regular operations following temporary gas supply
 disruptions
 * Free cash flow of NOK 1.4 billion impacted by higher metal prices and
 associated working capital requirements and prepayments
 * First metal produced at HalZero test facility, marking important milestone
 for carbon-free technology track
 * Commercial momentum continues for Hydro's low-carbon and recycled aluminium
 portfolio
 * New PPAs secured, further strengthening Hydro's long-term power position
Hydro delivered strong profitability in the quarter, with adjusted earnings per
share increasing from NOK 1.0 in the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 2.3 in the
third quarter of 2026. Free cash flow was NOK 1.4 billion, as strong adjusted
EBITDA was partly offset by higher net operating capital, primarily driven by
increased metal prices and associated working capital requirements and
prepayments. While this development reflects the current market environment,
improving cash conversion and working capital efficiency remains a clear
priority going forward. Consequently, Hydro has updated its year-end capex
guiding to around NOK 12.5 billion, down from NOK 13.5 billion, and net working
capital guiding to around NOK 32 billion, up from NOK 30 billion. The twelve
month adjusted RoaCE ended at 12.5 percent.
"Hydro's third quarter results reflect strong operational performance amplified
by market tailwinds. Record high liquid metal production from our Norwegian
smelter system, combined with strong pricing throughout the quarter drove solid
earnings and strong profitability. Operational excellence enables us to capture
more of the upside when markets are strong and, more importantly, builds
resilience when markets turn," says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of
Hydro.
During the third quarter, disruption in natural gas supplies to Alunorte
temporarily reduced production at the refinery. Through mitigating actions,
including securing alternative LNG supply, Hydro maintained operational
continuity and successfully restored alumina production.
Aluminium Metal benefited from higher all-in metal prices and strong operational
performance, while Recycling and Extrusions delivered improved earnings
supported by strong recycling margins. Hydro's Norwegian smelters increased
liquid metal production to record levels, reinforcing Hydro's position as a
reliable supplier of low-carbon aluminium to European customers.
In parallel, Hydro experienced continued momentum for its low-carbon and
recycled products, with leading brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty,
General Motors, and Mercedes-Benz integrating Hydro's solutions in their product
lines.
"We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from
some of the world's leading consumer brands. When brands like CHANEL Fragrances
and Beauty and Mercedes-Benz choose Hydro, they place their trust in our
quality, reliability, and ability to help them achieve their ambitions. That
trust has commercial value and reinforces our confidence in the long-term
opportunities for low-carbon and recycled aluminium," says Kallevik.
Hydro reached an important milestone in the development of its HalZero
technology by producing aluminium for the first time, demonstrating the core
electrolysis technology beyond laboratory scale. The achievement marks an
important step toward Hydro's long-term ambition of eliminating emissions from
electrolysis and anode production. Further testing, piloting and technology
development remain before any potential industrial application. Enova awarded
NOK 82 million in funding to support the concept development and planning of an
industrial concept pilot.
"This is an important milestone and a significant step forward in the
development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates that the
electrolysis technology works and paves the way for the continued development of
a game changing technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium
production in the future," says Kallevik.
During the quarter, Slovalco began the restart of primary aluminium production
following the agreement announced in July on long-term framework conditions with
the Slovak government. The restart commenced in late August, marking the return
of capacity curtailed during the European energy crisis in 2022. The first phase
targets an annual production capacity of 75,000 tonnes by the end of February
2027. The restart reflects the importance of competitive power, predictable
regulatory frameworks, and effective industrial policy in maintaining and
rebuilding Europe's industrial base.
Results and market development per business area
Adjusted EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina decreased compared to the third quarter of
last year, to NOK 283 million from NOK 1,290 million, mainly driven by lower
alumina sales prices, natural gas supply disruptions resulting in higher LNG
sourcing costs and unfavourable BRL/USD exchange rate effects.This was partly
offset by lower raw material costs and lower fixed costs.

title: TOMRA: 3Q26 - 20% revenue growth with strong operational performance
body:
Financial highlights 3rd quarter 2026
(comparison figures are from the corresponding period last year, modest currency
effects mainly in Collection)
 - Revenues were 366 MEUR, up 20% in TOMRA Group (3Q25: 306 MEUR). Revenues
were:
 - up 21% in Collection driven by 19% growth in existing markets and
continued new-market activity
 - up 34% in Recycling against a weak comparison quarter
 - up 13% in Food driven by several categories
 - Gross margin of 43.0% (3Q25: 44.1%) driven by business mix effects in
Collection
 - Operating expenses (adj. for special items) was 110 MEUR (3Q25: 104 MEUR),
up 5% driven by ramp-up in UK and Poland, FX, inflation and the addition of
Clynk
 - There were no special items in the quarter (3Q25: 0.0 MEUR)
 - EBITA (adj. for special items) was 47 MEUR (3Q25: 30 MEUR), up 55%
 - EPS (adj. for special items) was 0.08 EUR (3Q25: 0.05 EUR), up 72%
 - Cash flow from operations was 112 MEUR (3Q25: 64 MEUR), up 75%
 - Recycling order intake 73 MEUR (3Q25: 42 MEUR), up 73% driven by 26 MEUR
exceptionally large Mining orders
 - Food order intake 75 MEUR (3Q25: 77 MEUR), -2% reflecting investment timing
in an otherwise healthy pipeline
Tove Andersen, President and CEO of TOMRA Systems ASA comments:
"TOMRA delivered strong operational performance in the third quarter, with Group
revenues increasing 20%, EBITA up 55% and cash flow from operations up 75%.
Collection continues to lead the growth, with revenues up 21% and strong 19%
growth in existing markets, alongside continued progress in new deposit markets.
Our strong position in established markets provides a solid foundation to
benefit from ongoing modernization and replacement cycles, while expanding
recurring revenues from our installed base. In the UK, the first installations
have started ahead of the main deployment in 2027."
"In Recycling, profitability continues to move in the right direction as our
operational improvements and cost actions take effect, although overall market
sentiment remains broadly unchanged. Order intake was 73 MEUR, including 26 MEUR
of exceptionally large Mining orders. The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste
Regulation (PPWR) is now applicable, strengthening the long-term regulatory
backdrop for recycling. In Food, order intake remained stable at 75 MEUR, while
our broad exposure across regions and categories provides resilience and the
healthy pipeline gives us confidence in improving order intake and backlog."
Revenues for the TOMRA Group were 366 MEUR in the quarter (3Q25: 306 MEUR), up
20%. Collection revenues grew 21% to 217 MEUR (3Q25: 179 MEUR) with 19% growth
in existing markets, driven by Germany, North America and Australia, including
Clynk and one-off effects from Canada. New markets contributed 24 MEUR, driven
by the DRS rollout in Poland Singapore, and Romania. In Recycling, revenues grew
34% to 54 MEUR (3Q25: 40 MEUR) across all segments except plastics recycling. In
Food, revenues increased 13% to 86 MEUR (3Q25: 76 MEUR) across several
categories including citrus, blueberries and vegetables, offsetting the
downcycle in potatoes.
The order intake in Recycling was 73 MEUR in the quarter (3Q25: 42 MEUR), up 73%
driven by 26 MEUR exceptionally large Mining orders. Metal shows good momentum,
while waste recovery and plastics recycling remain soft but stable. In Food the
order intake was marginally down -2% to 75 MEUR (3Q25: 77 MEUR).
Gross margin for TOMRA Group was 43.0% in the quarter (3Q25: 44.1%), down on mix
-effects in Collection despite improvement in Recycling. In Collection, business
mix effects and high equipment sales in existing and new markets led to a gross
margin of 40.8% (3Q25: 42.3%). In Recycling, the gross margin improved to 47.7%
(3Q25: 43.9%) supported by higher volumes and COGS savings. Gross margin was
45.0% in Food, broadly stable year on year (3Q25: 45.1%), with positive volume
effects offset by product-mix differences.
Operating expenses increased 5% to 110 MEUR in the quarter (3Q25: 104 MEUR),
driven by ramp-up in UK, Poland, FX, inflation and the addition of Clynk.
The resulting EBITA adj. was EUR 47 MEUR (3Q25: 30 MEUR), up 55% with an EBITA
adj. margin of 12.9% (3Q25: 10.0%).

title: Gjensidige Q3 2026: Høyere lønnsomhet drevet av et forbedret forsikringsresultat
body:
Gjensidige leverte et resultat etter skatt på 2 076,7 millioner kroner i tredje
kvartal. God underliggende drift og gunstig skadeutvikling bidro til bedre
marginer og en betydelig økning i forsikringsresultatet fra skadeforsikring
sammenlignet med samme periode i fjor. Egenkapitalavkastningen økte til 34,2
prosent. Gjensidiges kapitalposisjon er sterk.
- Jeg er glad for å kunne rapportere nok et solid kvartal for Gjensidige, med
fortsatt vekst og god drift. Bak resultatene våre ligger innsatsen til mer enn 4
000 dedikerte medarbeidere på tvers av konsernet. Hver dag jobber de for å være
der når det gjelder som mest for kundene våre, en innsats som gjenspeiles i høy
kundetilfredshet og kundelojalitet. Tidligere denne uken fikk dette
anerkjennelse i Ipsos' årlige omdømmeundersøkelse, der Gjensidige ble rangert
høyest blant norske banker og forsikringsselskaper, sier konsernsjef Geir
Holmgren.
I juli opplevde Norge en av de største boligbrannene i moderne tid. Mer enn
hundre boliger ble ødelagt i Drammen-regionen, og mange familier mistet hjemmene
og eiendelene sine.
- Hendelser som denne minner oss om hvorfor forsikring er viktig. Selv om vi

kundeopplevelsen vi ønsker å tilby: tett personlig oppfølging der det best

title: Gjensidige Q3 2026: Higher profit driven by an improved insurance service result
body:
Gjensidige generated a profit after tax of NOK 2,076.7 million in the third
quarter. Strong operations and a favourable claims development supported
improved margins and resulted in a significant year-on-year increase in the
insurance service result from general insurance. The annualised return on equity
increased to 34.2 per cent. The capital position remains strong.
"I am pleased to report another solid quarter for Gjensidige, with continued
growth and strong operational performance. Our results are made possible by the
efforts of more than 4,000 dedicated colleagues across the Group. Every day,
they work to be there when it matters most for our customers, a commitment
reflected in high levels of customer satisfaction and retention. Earlier this
week, this was further recognised in Ipsos' annual reputation survey, where
Gjensidige ranked highest among Norwegian banks and insurance companies." says
CEO Geir Holmgren.
In July, Norway experienced one of the largest residential fire events in modern
times. More than one hundred homes were destroyed in the Drammen region, and
many families lost their homes and personal belongings.
"Events like this remind us why insurance matters. While we cannot prevent them,
we can provide predictability, financial security and practical support in
difficult situations. Our response illustrates the customer experience we aim to
provide: close personal support when customers need it, combined with fast and
convenient digital solutions when they value simplicity," says Holmgren.
Highlights third quarter 2026 (third quarter 2025):
 - Insurance revenue from general insurance: NOK 11,367.4 million (11,201.9)
 - Insurance service result general insurance: NOK 3,003.6 million (2,270.6)
 - Financial result investment portfolio: Negative NOK 192.9 million (534.0)
 - Profit before tax expense: NOK 2,780.6 million (2,067.4)
 - Loss ratio, net of reinsurance: 62.0% (68.9%)
 - Cost ratio: 11.5% (10.8%)
 - Combined ratio: 73.6% (79.7%)
 - Underlying frequency loss ratio, net of reinsurance: 60.1% (65.7%)
 - Earnings per share from continuing operations: NOK 4.08 (3.04)
 - Solvency ratio: 190% (189% Q2 2026)
Insurance revenue from general insurance increased by 1.5 per cent to NOK
11,367.4 million (11,201.9) in the quarter, or by 3.7 per cent measured in local
currency. Adjusted for the non-recurring effect related to change in revenue
recognition for home seller insurance policies in Private Norway last year, the
growth was 5.3 per cent. The increase was mainly driven by pricing measures
across the Private and Commercial portfolios in all geographies and higher
volumes for property, accident and health and travel insurance in Private
Norway.
The general insurance service result was NOK 3,003.6 million (2,270.6). The
improvement was driven by lower loss ratios in both the Private and Commercial
segments.
Pension
The pension segment recorded a profit before tax adjusted for the contractual
service margin (CSM) of NOK 98.2 million (negative 362.0). Adjusted for last
year's non-recurring termination expense, profit before tax adjusted for CSM
improved by NOK 25.4 million, reflecting a higher insurance service result
adjusted for CSM, partly offset by lower net finance income.
Financial result
The financial result for the investment portfolios was negative NOK 192.9
million (534.0). Net of insurance finance (unwinding and changes in financial
assumptions), the net financial result for the investment portfolio was negative
NOK 24.6 million (440.8). Higher interest rates during the period as well as
higher credit spreads contributed negatively to the result.

Reference is made to the recommended voluntary cash offer by Fortum Consumer Solutions AS (the "Offeror"), a company wholly owned by Fortum Oyj ("Fortum"), to acquire all issued and outstanding shares in Elmera Group ASA ("Elmera"), except for shares owned by Elmera, at a price of NOK 47 per share on the terms and conditions set out in the offer document dated 20 August 2026 (the "Offer Document") (the "Offer"). Reference is further made to the stock exchange announcement published on 2 October 2026 regarding settlement notification and results of the Offer.
The Offeror announces that settlement of the Offer has been completed.
Following settlement of the Offer, the Offeror holds 105,108,968 shares, representing approximately 91.92% of the issued and outstanding share capital and voting rights of Elmera (96.12% excluding Elmera's treasury shares).
Following completion of the Offer, the Offeror intends to carry out a compulsory acquisition of the remaining shares not owned by Elmera or the Offeror at a redemption price equal to the offer price in the Offer of NOK 47 per share, pursuant to Section 4-25 of the Norwegian Limited Liability Companies Act and Section 6-22 of the Norwegian Securities Trading Act.
