title: Correction: Norsk Hydro: Solide resultater og god drift
body:
Hydros justerte EBITDA var 9.089 millioner kroner i tredje kvartal 2026, en
økning fra 5.996 millioner kroner i samme kvartal i fjor. Høyere all-in
metallpriser og høyere aluminapriser bidro positivt, sammen med bedre inntjening
i Recycling og Extrusions. Resultatet ble delvis utlignet av høyere anode- og
energikostnader i Aluminium Metal, økte energikostnader i Bauxite & Alumina
grunnet forstyrrelser i gassforsyningen, en sterkere norsk krone i forhold til
USD, og tap på forskjeller mellom prisområder i Energy.
 * Alunorte startet opp normal drift etter midlertidige forstyrrelser i
 gassforsyningen
 * Fri kontantstrøm på 1,4 milliarder kroner påvirket av høyere metallpriser og
 tilhørende krav til arbeidskapital og forskuddsbetalinger
 * Første metallproduksjon ved testanlegget HalZero, en viktig milepæl i
 utviklingen av karbonfri teknologi
 * Den kommersielle utviklingen fortsetter for Hydros portefølje av lavkarbon-
 og resirkulert aluminium
 * Nye langsiktige avtaler om kraftkjøp (PPA) er inngått og styrker Hydros
 langsiktige kraftposisjon ytterligere
Hydro hadde høy lønnsomhet i kvartalet, og justert resultat per aksje har økt
fra 1,00 kroner i tredje kvartal 2025 til 2,30 kroner i tredje kvartal 2026. Fri
kontantstrøm var 1,4 milliarder kroner, med en høy justert EBITDA som ble delvis
utlignet av høyere netto driftskapital, i hovedsak drevet av økte metallpriser,
tilhørende krav til arbeidskapital og forskuddsbetalinger. Selv om denne
utviklingen reflekterer dagens markedsforhold, vil det legges betydelig vekt på
kontantstrøm og økt effektivitet i styring av arbeidskapital i tiden framover.
Som følge av dette har Hydro redusert investeringsmålet ved utgangen av året fra
13,5 milliarder kroner til rundt 12,5 milliarder kroner, og økt antatt netto
arbeidskapital fra 30 milliarder kroner til rundt 32 milliarder kroner. Justert
RoaCE over de siste tolv månedene endte på 12,5 prosent.
- Hydros resultater for tredje kvartal reflekterer god drift, som ble forsterket
av gunstige markedsforhold. Rekordhøy produksjon av flytende metall fra de
norske verkene og høye priser i hele kvartalet har gitt solid inntjening og høy
lønnsomhet. God drift gjør at vi kan utnytte mer av oppsiden når
markedsforholdene er gode og ikke minst gjør det oss mer robuste når markedet
snur, sier Hydros konsernsjef, Eivind Kallevik.
I tredje kvartal oppsto det forstyrrelser i forsyningen av naturgass til
Alunorte, noe som førte til en midlertidig reduksjon i produksjonen ved
raffineriet. Basert på ulike tiltak, inkludert gjennom å sikre alternativ
forsyning av LNG, var Hydro i stand til å opprettholde driften og gjenoppta
produksjonen av alumina.
Aluminium Metal dro fordel av høyere all-in metallpriser og solid drift, mens
Recycling og Extrusions hadde bedre inntjening som følge av høye
resirkuleringsmarginer. De norske metallverkene økte produksjonen av flytende
metall til et rekordhøyt nivå, og befester Hydros posisjon som en pålitelig
leverandør av lavkarbonaluminium til europeiske kunder.
Samtidig opplever Hydro fortsatt framgang for lavkarbon- og resirkulerte
produkter, med ledende merkenavn som CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty, General
Motors og Mercedes-Benz, som bruker Hydros løsninger i sitt sortiment.
- Vi ser fortsatt stor etterspørsel etter våre lavkarbon- og resirkulerte
produkter fra noen av verdens ledende forbrukermerker. Når merkenavn som CHANEL
Fragrances and Beauty og Mercedes-Benz velger Hydro, har de tillit til vår
kvalitet, pålitelighet og evne til å hjelpe dem å nå sine ambisjoner. Den
tilliten har kommersiell verdi, og styrker vår tro på de langsiktige mulighetene
for lavkarbon- og resirkulert aluminium, sier Kallevik
Hydro nådde en viktig milepæl i utviklingen av sin HalZero-teknologi med
produksjon av aluminium for første gang, og utprøving av elektrolyseteknologien
utover laboratorieskala. Denne milepælen er et viktig steg på veien i Hydros
langsiktige ambisjon om utslippsfri elektrolyse- og anodeproduksjon. Det
gjenstår ytterligere testing, pilotprøving og teknologiutvikling før eventuell
bruk i industriell skala. Enova har innvilget 82 millioner kroner til
konseptutvikling og planlegging av en industrielt pilotanlegg.
- Dette er en viktig milepæl og et viktig steg på veien i utviklingen av
HalZero. Denne første produksjonen av metall viser at elektrolyseteknologien
fungerer, og åpner for fortsatt utvikling av en banebrytende teknologi som kan
gi utslippsfri produksjon av aluminium i framtiden, sier Kallevik.
I kvartalet begynte Slovalco arbeidet med å starte opp igjen produksjonen av
primæraluminium, etter en avtale om langsiktige rammebetingelser med den
slovakiske regjeringen som ble kunngjort i juli. Produksjonen ble startet sent i
august, og innebærer at kapasitet som ble stengt ned i forbindelse med den
europeiske energikrisen i 2022 nå blir tilbakeført. I den første fasen tas det
sikte på en årlig produksjonskapasitet på 75.000 tonn innen utgangen av februar
2027. Oppstarten reflekterer betydningen av konkurransedyktig kraft,
forutsigbare rammebetingelser og en effektiv industripolitikk som kan
opprettholde og gjenoppbygge industrigrunnlaget i Europa.
Resultater og markedsutvikling i forretningsområdene
Justert EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina gikk ned fra 1.290 millioner kroner til
283 millioner kroner, sammenlignet med tredje kvartal i fjor. Nedgangen skyldtes
hovedsakelig lavere aluminapriser, forstyrrelser i naturgassforsyningen som ga
høyere kostnader knyttet til kjøp av LNG, og ugunstige valutaeffekter i
kursforholdet mellom BRL/USD. Dette ble delvis motvirket av lavere
råvarekostnader og lavere faste kostnader.
Prisene på Platts aluminaindeks (PAX) gikk opp i tredje kvartal 2026, til 370
USD ved utgangen av kvartalet, noe som avvek fra kinesiske aluminapriser, som
gikk ned. Til tross for lavere aluminaproduksjon ved enkelte raffinerier i
Indonesia grunnet utfordringer med råvareforsyning, var det et overskudd i
markedet utenom Kina i kvartalet. Kinas aluminamarked fikk stadig stør

title: Correction: Norsk Hydro: Solid results and strong performance
body:
Hydro's adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 9,089 million, up
from NOK 5,996 million in the same quarter last year. Higher all-in metal prices
and higher alumina prices contributed positively in the quarter, along with
improved earnings in Recycling and Extrusions. The strong performance was
partially offset by higher anode and energy costs in Aluminium Metal, increased
energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions, a stronger NOK
vs USD, and negative price area differences in Energy.
 * Alunorte resumed regular operations following temporary gas supply
 disruptions
 * Free cash flow of NOK 1.4 billion impacted by higher metal prices and
 associated working capital requirements and prepayments
 * First metal produced at HalZero test facility, marking important milestone
 for carbon-free technology track
 * Commercial momentum continues for Hydro's low-carbon and recycled aluminium
 portfolio
 * New PPAs secured, further strengthening Hydro's long-term power position
Hydro delivered strong profitability in the quarter, with adjusted earnings per
share increasing from NOK 1.0 in the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 2.3 in the
third quarter of 2026. Free cash flow was NOK 1.4 billion, as strong adjusted
EBITDA was partly offset by higher net operating capital, primarily driven by
increased metal prices and associated working capital requirements and
prepayments. While this development reflects the current market environment,
improving cash conversion and working capital efficiency remains a clear
priority going forward. Consequently, Hydro has updated its year-end capex
guiding to around NOK 12.5 billion, down from NOK 13.5 billion, and net working
capital guiding to around NOK 32 billion, up from NOK 30 billion. The twelve
month adjusted RoaCE ended at 12.5 percent.
"Hydro's third quarter results reflect strong operational performance amplified
by market tailwinds. Record high liquid metal production from our Norwegian
smelter system, combined with strong pricing throughout the quarter drove solid
earnings and strong profitability. Operational excellence enables us to capture
more of the upside when markets are strong and, more importantly, builds
resilience when markets turn," says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of
Hydro.
During the third quarter, disruption in natural gas supplies to Alunorte
temporarily reduced production at the refinery. Through mitigating actions,
including securing alternative LNG supply, Hydro maintained operational
continuity and successfully restored alumina production.
Aluminium Metal benefited from higher all-in metal prices and strong operational
performance, while Recycling and Extrusions delivered improved earnings
supported by strong recycling margins. Hydro's Norwegian smelters increased
liquid metal production to record levels, reinforcing Hydro's position as a
reliable supplier of low-carbon aluminium to European customers.
In parallel, Hydro experienced continued momentum for its low-carbon and
recycled products, with leading brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty,
General Motors, and Mercedes-Benz integrating Hydro's solutions in their product
lines.
"We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from
some of the world's leading consumer brands. When brands like CHANEL Fragrances
and Beauty and Mercedes-Benz choose Hydro, they place their trust in our
quality, reliability, and ability to help them achieve their ambitions. That
trust has commercial value and reinforces our confidence in the long-term
opportunities for low-carbon and recycled aluminium," says Kallevik.
Hydro reached an important milestone in the development of its HalZero
technology by producing aluminium for the first time, demonstrating the core
electrolysis technology beyond laboratory scale. The achievement marks an
important step toward Hydro's long-term ambition of eliminating emissions from
electrolysis and anode production. Further testing, piloting and technology
development remain before any potential industrial application. Enova awarded
NOK 82 million in funding to support the concept development and planning of an
industrial concept pilot.
"This is an important milestone and a significant step forward in the
development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates that the
electrolysis technology works and paves the way for the continued development of
a game changing technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium
production in the future," says Kallevik.
During the quarter, Slovalco began the restart of primary aluminium production
following the agreement announced in July on long-term framework conditions with
the Slovak government. The restart commenced in late August, marking the return
of capacity curtailed during the European energy crisis in 2022. The first phase
targets an annual production capacity of 75,000 tonnes by the end of February
2027. The restart reflects the importance of competitive power, predictable
regulatory frameworks, and effective industrial policy in maintaining and
rebuilding Europe's industrial base.
Results and market development per business area
Adjusted EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina decreased compared to the third quarter of
last year, to NOK 283 million from NOK 1,290 million, mainly driven by lower
alumina sales prices, natural gas supply disruptions resulting in higher LNG
sourcing costs and unfavourable BRL/USD exchange rate effects.This was partly
offset by lower raw material costs and lower fixed costs.
PAX traded up throughout the third quarter 2026 to USD 370 per mt at the end on
the quarter, diverging from Chinese alumina prices moving down. Despite lower
alumina production at certain refineries in Indonesia because of raw material

quarter. China's alumina market became increasingly oversupplied during the
quarter as new refinery capacity came on line. Chinese alumina p

body:
The Board of Directors of BW Energy Limited ("BWE" or the "Company") approved
the award of share options under a Long-Term Incentive Program (LTIP) to align
the interests of the participating employees with those of the Company's
shareholders. The LTIP is discretionary, and participants are invited on an
annual basis.
The total number of shares awarded under the LTIP for 2026 is 1,120,000,
allocated to options that will give the holder the right to acquire one BW
Energy share per option. A total of nine BW Energy employees have been invited
to participate in the program.
The strike price of the options is calculated based on the volume-weighted
average share price five trading days prior to the grant date, plus a premium
of 15.75% (corresponding to a 5% increase annually over three years). The
strike price for the options awarded on 25 February 2026 is NOK 56.237.
The options will have a vesting period of three years, followed by a
three-year exercise period. Options shall be exercisable from vesting to the
expiration of the three-year exercise period, other than during any restricted
period. The options will expire six years after the award date.
The options are non-tradable and conditional upon the option holder being
employed by the Company and not having resigned or being terminated for cause
prior to the vesting date.
Following the new awards, the Company will have a total of 6,623,400
outstanding options.
The following primary insiders of the Company have been awarded options under
the LTIP for 2026:
1. Chief Executive Officer, Carl K. Arnet has been awarded 500,000 options.
Following the award Carl K. Arnet has a total number of 3,800,000 options.

Veidekke: Skal bygge storprosjekt for Thon Gruppen på Storo
Veidekke: Awarded major project for Thon Gruppen at Storo
body:
Veidekke has been selected to construct a combined residential, office and
commercial development for Thon Gruppen at Vitaminveien 6 in the Storo district
of Oslo. The design and build contract is valued at approximately NOK 745
million, excluding VAT.
Jimmy Bengtsson, Group Chief Executive of Veidekke, and Kjetil Nilsen, Group CEO
of Thon Gruppen, signed the contract on Friday, 23 October.
"This is a large and exciting project that we are delighted to deliver together
with Thon Gruppen. Vitaminveien 6 combines residential, office and commercial
space in a single development and is an excellent match for our expertise in
large and complex construction projects. We look forward to a strong partnership
and to contributing to the continued development of Storo," says Jimmy
Bengtsson, Group Chief Executive of Veidekke.
For the client, Thon Eiendom, this is an important project that is now moving
forward to the construction phase.
"We are developing this property with a long-term ownership and management
perspective, and that influences the choices we make from the outset. This
applies to everything from the energy solutions to the rooftop garden that will
be shared by residents and office tenants. With Veidekke, we gain a partner with
extensive experience from demanding and complex developments," says Kjetil
Nilsen, Group CEO of Thon Gruppen.
Vitaminveien 6 will be an important contribution to the ongoing transformation
of Storo into a modern urban district. The development comprises an office
building with its main façade facing Vitaminveien, a residential building to the
west, and a commercial podium connecting the two.
The project has a total gross floor area of approximately 30,000 square metres.
It includes a podium structure extending both above and below ground,
accommodating parking facilities and retail premises. A seven-storey residential
building and a seven-storey office building will be constructed on top of the
podium. The residential section will comprise 98 rental apartments, while the
office building will provide approximately 5,200 square metres of gross floor
area (GFA).
A key objective of the project is to create attractive green spaces. The
development will include a rooftop garden and landscaped park areas on top of
the commercial podium, creating a shared courtyard for residents and office
users. Additional green areas will also be established at ground level.
The office building will be certified to BREEAM Excellent and achieve Energy
Performance Certificate (EPC) Class A.
Demolition of the existing buildings is scheduled to begin in November, while
construction of the new Vitaminveien 6 development is expected to commence in
April 2027. The project is scheduled for completion in August 2029. The contract
will be included in Veidekke's order backlog for the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: Endúr ASA - BMO to acquire Notech
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
26 October 2026 - BMO Entreprenør AS ("BMO"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Endúr ASA ("Endúr"), is happy to announce its planned acquisition of 100% of the shares in Notech AS ("Notech"/"The Company").
Notech is a mechanical steel contractor, supplying fabricated steel products, services and personnel to infrastructure, industrial and offshore markets. The Company operates workshop and office facilities in Larvik and Sandefjord, Norway, respectively, and employs approximately 80 people. Notech has been a highly valued and trusted partner to BMO for many years, providing engineering and steel bridges for BMO's numerous successful bridge replacement projects for Bane NOR. Notech has also supplied steel structures for major construction projects undertaken by HAB Construction. The acquisition secures continuity in critical delivery capacity, creates opportunities for expanded collaboration on fabricated steel products for Endúr's other subsidiaries, and provides further exposure to stable and profitable markets and clients within infrastructure, industry and offshore.
Founder and General Manager, Dag Abrahamsen, holds 100% of Notech and will remain in his current position following the completion of the transaction. Notech will continue to operate as an independent company, but in close partnership with BMO.
"We are incredibly excited to secure an even closer and longer-term partnership with an organization and people we know to be highly skilled, profitable and loyal. Notech is a quality company in every respect", says Aleksander Rød, General Manager of BMO.
The acquisition values The Company at a base enterprise value on cash- and debt-free basis, excluding leasing liabilities ("Base EV") of NOK 120 million. The Company expects to report FY 2026 revenues of around NOK ~185-195 million (FY 2025: NOK 204.8 million), with an operating result ("EBIT") of around NOK ~20 million (FY 2025: NOK 39.1 million) and a margin of ~10-11% (FY 2025: 19.1%). In addition to a sound strategic rationale, the acquisition will be highly accretive with an implied EV/EBIT multiple of 6x. The acquisition adds approximately NOK ~50 million to Endúr's existing backlog.
The Base EV may be adjusted upwards or downwards by an additional consideration of up to NOK +35/-20 million ("The Additional Consideration"), to be settled by 30 June 2029. Within this range, The Additional Consideration will be calculated as the difference between cumulative EBIT for the 2026-2028 period and a target of NOK 60 million, multiplied by 2x. This adjustment mechanism ensures an EV/EBIT multiple of 6x for an average EBIT during the 2026-2028 period within a range of NOK 16.7-25.6 million.
The acquisition will be partly financed with a NOK 20 million seller's credit, to be settled by 30 June 2029 and offsetable against any negative Additional Consideration. The seller will also receive consideration shares in Endúr of NOK 40.1 million, valued at the shares' volume weighted average price ("VWAP") on The Oslo Stock Exhange for the last 15 trading days leading up to this announcement. The consideration shares will be subject to lock-up restrictions, being released with 1/3 at each of 12, 18 and 24 months after closing.
"We are pleased with the compelling strategic and financial rationale behind this investment. The transaction is another clear example of our stated ambition to continue growing through accretive M&A, which will remain a defining feature of Endúr going forward, on both short and long term", says Jeppe Raaholt, CEO of Endúr.
A signed share purchase agreement ("SPA") is in place and the acquisition is expected to close during Q4 in 2026, with completion being subject to approval from The Norwegian Competition Authority and certain other customary conditions.
Advokatfirmaet Bull acted as legal advisor to Endúr.
For further comments, contact:
Media:
Aleksander Rød, General Manager of BMO: +47 994 61 454
Jeppe Raaholt, CEO of Endúr: +47 976 69 759
Investors:
Einar Olsen, CFO of Endúr: +47 924 01 787
(ENDS)
About Endúr:
Endúr ASA (XOSL: ENDUR) is a leading Scandinavian contractor headquartered in Lysaker and listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange. The company specializes in critical infrastructure, including bridges, quays, tunnels, and dams. Operating as a disciplined serial acquirer (compounder), the group utilizes a decentralized model that grants subsidiaries high autonomy to preserve their technical expertise and local market positions. Endúr drives long-term value through strategic platform acquisitions and targeted bolt-ons in fragmented niche markets.

body:
SSEA, a subsidiary of Sentia, has today signed an agreement with Gällivare
Municipality for additional time-critical works at the Multi-Activity Centre
in Gällivare. The contract value is approximately SEK 340 million, excluding
VAT. This is the third order for time-critical works in the project.
The order secures progress on the project while negotiations on the contract
for phase 2 continue. The phase 2 contract was previously expected to be
signed in mid-2026. It is now expected to be signed by year-end.
-We have a good collaboration with Gällivare Municipality, and this order
ensures the project keeps its pace. We look forward to finalising phase 2 and
continuing our work on a building that will become an important meeting place
for the entire municipality, says Christian Wieland, Deputy CEO Sentia and EVP
Sentia Sweden.
The Multi-Activity Centre will include an experience pool, sports and bowling
halls, a cinema, a library and cultural venues, with a total gross floor area
of approximately 20,600 square metres (GFA). The project is expected to be
completed in 2029.

title: Pressemelding Q3 2026: SATS vokser videre - åpner 18 nye treningssentre
body:
SATS fortsetter den sterke utviklingen i tredje kvartal 2026. Omsetningen økte
med 7 prosent valutajustert til 1 324 millioner kroner, mens driftsresultatet
(EBIT) steg med 35 prosent valutajustert til 182 millioner kroner. Med 18 nye
treningssentre planlagt åpnet innen utgangen av 2028 vil SATS gjøre det
enklere for enda flere i Norden å finne treningsgleden.
EBITDA økte med 25 prosent valutajustert til 235 millioner kroner, drevet av
at inntektene vokste raskere enn kostnadene. Etter flere kvartaler med solid
lønnsomhetsutvikling har SATS bygget et sterkt fundament for videre vekst,
både gjennom utvikling av eksisterende sentre og med en ambisjon om å åpne
8-12 nye sentre årlig fremover.
- Vi er stolte av de sterke resultatene vi leverer, men det som virkelig
driver oss, er å inspirere flere til å oppleve treningsglede og mestring. Med
18 nye sentre på trappene gleder vi oss til å ønske enda flere velkommen til
SATS, sier Sondre Gravir, konsernsjef i SATS.
Stadig flere finner treningsgleden sammen
Treningsaktiviteten blant SATS-medlemmene fortsetter å øke. I tredje kvartal
deltok 6 prosent flere medlemmer på gruppetrening sammenlignet med samme
periode i fjor.
- Det er utrolig inspirerende å se at flere finner veien til gruppetimene
våre. Vi vet hvor mye fellesskap og mestring betyr for motivasjonen til å
fortsette å trene. For mange er det nettopp det å trene sammen med andre som
gjør at trening blir en naturlig og positiv del av hverdagen, sier Gravir.

body:
Limassol, Cyprus -- 27 October, 2026 -- Energy Drilling, a wholly owned
subsidiary of SED Energy Holdings Plc ("Energy Holdings"), has received a
letter of award from Carigali-PTTEPI Operating Company Sdn. Bhd. ("CPOC") for
a 30-month offshore drilling campaign, with options for up to an additional 15
months, for its tender-assist drilling rig T-16 in Malaysia. The firm contract
period has an estimated value of approximately USD 87 million including
mobilization fees.
"This award confirms the strong demand we are seeing across Southeast Asia and
demonstrates Energy Drilling's ability to win attractive long-term work with
leading customers. By securing firm employment for T-16 into 2030, we add
meaningfully to our backlog and strengthen our long-term earnings visibility
and distribution capacity," said Kurt M. Waldeland, CEO of Energy Holdings.
The award covers Phase 7 of CPOC's development campaign in the
Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area. The T-16 is currently completing
Phase 6 of the same campaign, with a firm term through December 2026 and
options for further extensions. Based on the latest estimates, the current
campaign is expected to conclude in Q1 2027 with Phase 7 expected to commence
early in Q3 2027. Following completion of the current campaign, T-16 will be
demobilized to Singapore, where the rig will be kept with reduced crewing and
operating costs ahead of the new campaign.
"This latest contract further strengthens our position in Malaysia and
reflects the confidence that CPOC continues to place in Energy Drilling's
execution capabilities," said Luc Plouzennec, CEO of Energy Drilling. "The
T-16 has consistently delivered strong operational performance on the field,
achieving high levels of reliability, efficiency and safety. Securing this
follow-on campaign builds on this proven track record and reinforces our
long-standing presence in one of our key markets."

title: Thor Medical and Medicines Discovery Catapult Enter Three-Year Supply Agreement to Accelerate Radiopharmaceutical Development in the UK
body:
27.10.2026 07:00:08 CET | Thor Medical ASA | Non-regulatory press releases
Thor Medical, a leading supplier of high-purity isotopes to the
radiopharmaceutical industry, has entered into a three-year supply agreement
with Medicines Discovery Catapult (MDC), a life science service dedicated to
turning drug discovery into commercial breakthroughs.
Under the agreement, Thor Medical will supply radium-224 (Ra-224) and lead-212
(Pb-212) from its industrial-scale AlphaOne facility. The agreement will support
MDC's wider work to accelerate the development of Pb-212- and Ra-224-based
radiopharmaceutical therapies in the UK. First shipments to MDC have already
been made.
"We are pleased to support Medicines Discovery Catapult with the isotopes it
needs to help advance radiopharmaceutical development in the UK. Since opening
AlphaOne, we are seeing increasing interest in securing predictable and stable
isotope supply, which is an important enabler for preclinical development. We
look forward to supporting MDC and the programmes it works with over the coming
years," said Jasper C. Kurth, CEO of Thor Medical.
With increasing investment in the development, manufacture, and clinical
translation of precision radiopharmaceutical medicines, a reliable supply of
medical isotopes remains fundamental to advancing research and development in
this space.
Alongside securing isotope supplies for development programmes, MDC is
supporting initiatives to strengthen the UK's future capability. This includes a
£18.8 million consortium, partially funded by Innovate UK's Sustainable
Medicines Manufacturing Innovation Programme and led by United Kingdom National
Nuclear Laboratory and Medicines Discovery Catapult, which is working to
establish the ecosystem of a UK Pb-212 supply chain.
Together, these activities help ensure innovators can access the isotopes they
need today while supporting the long-term growth of UK radiopharmaceutical
capability.
"This agreement with Thor Medical strengthens MDC's ability to support
radiopharmaceutical developers in getting precision treatments closer to
patients. By combining isotope supply with MDC's preclinical development
capabilities, we can help partners generate the evidence needed to progress
programmes from early discovery to clinical development and future impact," said
Dr. Juliana Maynard, Chief Scientist, Translational Imaging and
Radiopharmaceuticals, Medicines Discovery Catapult.
ENDS

ABOUT THOR MEDICAL ASA
Thor Medical is a leading supplier of high-purity isotopes to the
radiopharmaceutical industry. The Company's proprietary production platform
combines advanced separation technology with industrial-scale manufacturing
capacity to deliver a reliable, scalable and cost-efficient supply of
alpha-emitting radioisotopes. Thor Medical supports radiopharmaceutical
companies from early-stage development to commercialization enabling scale-up of
next-generation targeted cancer therapies.
Thor Medical's product portfolio includes lead-212 (Pb-212) and its precursor
isotopes thorium-228 (Th-228) and radium-224 (Ra-224). Based on naturally
occurring thorium, Thor Medical's production process requires neither
irradiation nor nuclear reactors, providing significant cost advantages while
minimizing radioactive waste.
Guided by its vision to become a world-leading enabler for targeted cancer
therapies, Thor Medical is committed to improving millions of lives by powering
the next generation of precision cancer treatment with high-purity isotopes.
Thor Medical is headquartered in Oslo, Norway, and listed on the Oslo Stock
Exchange under the ticker symbol TRMED. For more information, visit

title: SATS ASA Q3 2026: Profit up on higher value per member
body:
SATS ASA delivered another quarter of solid earnings growth in Q3 2026. EBITDA
before IFRS 16 rose 22% to NOK 235 million, EBIT before IFRS 16 increased 33%
to NOK 182 million, and earnings per share came in at NOK 0.69, compared with
NOK 0.48 a year ago. Higher value per member drove the improvement, with ARPM
up 7% currency adjusted and more members taking part in group training.
Alongside the results, SATS has updated its capital allocation framework,
widening the leverage target to 1.0x-2.0x net debt to EBITDA before IFRS 16,
and clarifying the ambition to raise the dividend per share over time. With 18
new clubs secured through 2028, SATS is moving from optimizing its club
portfolio to also growing it.
Key highlights from the third quarter of 2026:
* Total revenues increased by 2% (+7% curr. adj.) to NOK 1 324 million in Q3
 2026, as ARPM rose by 2% (+7% curr. adj.), while the number of clubs fell
 from 274 to 268 and the member base declined by 0.5%
* Revenues grew faster than costs, lifting EBITDA before IFRS 16 by 22% (+25%
 curr. adj.) to NOK 235 million
* EBIT before IFRS 16 of NOK 182 million, 33% (+35% curr. adj.) above Q3 2025
* Earnings per share grew 43% to NOK 0.69, from NOK 0.48 in the same quarter
 last year
* Free cash flow of NOK 132 million in Q3 2026 and NOK 609 million over twelve
 months, with leverage steady at 1.1x for the fourth quarter in a row
* Members train more often, with workouts rising 2%, and group training
 workouts rising 4% on top of 10% growth in Q3 2025
* NOK 193 million was returned to shareholders in Q3 through dividends and
 share buybacks
"More people are joining our group classes, and they come back more often.
Group training workouts grew 4% this quarter, on top of 10% last year, and
active members are the members who stay with us. That loyalty is what makes
our earnings growth steady, quarter after quarter," says Sondre Gravir, CEO of
SATS.

title: Elopak s third quarter (Q3): Regaining momentum despite ongoing headwinds
body:
Elopak ASA ("Elopak", Oslo Børs Ticker: ELO) reports encouraging progress
across several parts of its business and continued improvements in financial
performance, despite a challenging operating environment.
Third quarter 2026 summary
* Group revenue increased by 6.5% year-on-year (+6.0% in constant currency),
 while EBITDA totaled EUR 51.9 million, with a margin of 16.8%
* EMEA delivered strong performance, with revenues rising 7.5%, supported by
 volume growth across Pure Pak® and Roll Fed in Europe
* Americas revenues increased 5.9%, despite growth being constrained by the
 board supply disruption following the Nippon Dynawave incident. Insurance
 recoveries recognized in the quarter partly compensated for the additional
 costs, with further recoveries expected
* ROCE increased to 15.4% while the leverage ratio remained stable at 2.2x
* Net profit attributable to Elopak shareholders was EUR 25.0 million, an
 increase of 38% compared with the corresponding quarter last year
* Håkon Volldal will assume the role of CEO effective November 2, 2026.
 Reinard Dreesmann has been appointed interim EVP Region Americas

resilient results demonstrate that we can continue to drive progress and
improvements through disciplined execution and a focused strategy. I am proud

title: Vend Marketplaces ASA: Interim report Q3 2026
body:
27.10.2026 07:00:09 CET | Vend Marketplaces ASA | Half year financial report
Today, Vend Marketplaces ASA ("Vend") released its Q3 2026 results.
Higher margins, lower costs and continued capital returns
"Our third-quarter results show further progress for a simpler Vend: revenue
growth, a lower cost base, higher margins and continued capital returns. But
there are also areas that require more work - notably the recovery of Blocket
and further improving cost efficiency. Over time, we see clear potential to keep
growing revenues while expanding margins," says CEO Christian Printzell
Halvorsen.
Halvorsen adds: 
"Group revenues were NOK 1,641 million, up 3% year on year or 6% in constant
currency. Our four verticals grew 11% in constant currency, partly offset by the
phase-out of transition service agreement revenues from the Schibsted
separation. Group EBITDA increased 11% to NOK 711 million, with the margin
expanding by around three percentage points to 43%.
Real Estate had a strong quarter, driven by continued ARPA growth in Norway. In
Recommerce, increased marketing and shipping incentives in Norway drove
accelerated GMV growth but weighed on profitability. Jobs grew as monetisation
gains more than offset a market-driven volume decline. In Mobility,
constant-currency revenue growth improved, with strong ARPA in Norway and
professional ARPA growth in Sweden back at double digits, and organisational
changes made at the end of the second quarter lifted the margin. However,
private volumes in Sweden are still declining year on year, and performance in
Denmark continued below our ambitions.
Our focus on cost is delivering ahead of what we indicated earlier in the year.
We now expect the 2026 cost base (OPEX excluding COGS) to decline by around NOK
250 million year on year, up from around NOK 150 million indicated at Q2, while
retaining the flexibility to reinvest in growth, as we are doing in Recommerce.
Year to date, our EBITDA margin is 40%, up from 27% in the same period of 2024,
but still below leading international marketplaces - and improving this remains
a key priority.
Our capital allocation remains focused on long-term value creation, and we have
returned excess capital consistently since 2024. The first NOK 2 billion tranche
of our current NOK 4 billion buyback was completed in August, and the second had
reached around NOK 1.4 billion as at 23 October. As announced on 26 October, we
are taking steps to enable continued share buybacks beyond the current
programme. Our 14% stake in Adevinta continues to develop well operationally,
and its valuation increased by NOK 3.9 billion in the quarter to NOK 11.1
billion.
Our view of AI as a meaningful opportunity for marketplaces has not changed. If
anything, we are more convinced. We continue to experiment broadly and scale
what works, and AI features are live across all our verticals. AI makes our
current products better, from AI-assisted listing creation and semantic search
in Recommerce to virtual staging and interactive floor plans in Real Estate and
AI recommendations for car dealers in Mobility. It also expands the range of
user and customer needs we can serve, such as home valuations for consumers on
FINN, an AI career coach for job seekers, and Agentic Apply, where an AI agent
helps candidates apply without leaving FINN. And AI agents will never be better
than the data they rely on - which makes our proprietary marketplace data,
trusted brands and direct user relationships increasingly valuable."
This quarter's highlights
 * Group: Revenues of NOK 1,641 million, up 3% YoY and 6% in constant currency,
 with the verticals up 11% in constant currency. EBITDA of NOK 711 million, up
 11%, with the margin up around 3 percentage points to 43%.
 * Mobility: Revenues up 4% YoY and 8% in constant currency, driven by
 professional ARPA growth in Norway and Sweden. EBITDA of NOK 406 million, up
 7%, with a margin of 59%.
 * Real Estate: Revenues up 12% YoY and 14% in constant currency, driven by 17%
 ARPA growth in FINN residential-for-sale. EBITDA of NOK 206 million, up 23%,
 with a margin of 53%.
 * Jobs: Revenues up 8% YoY, as ARPA growth of 11% more than offset a 3% decline
 in volumes. EBITDA of NOK 146 million, up 7%, with a margin of 55%.
 * Recommerce: Revenues up 12% YoY and 16% in constant currency, with record
 transaction volumes of 1.9 million, up 31%. EBITDA of NOK -43 million, down
 NOK 8 million, reflecting increased marketing and shipping incentives in
 Norway.
 * Capital allocation: The first NOK 2 billion tranche of the current NOK 4
 billion share buyback programme was completed in August, and the second had
 reached around NOK 1.4 billion as at 23 October. As announced on 26 October,
 we are taking steps to enable continued share buybacks beyond the current
 programme.
 * Adevinta: Valuation revised to NOK 11.1 billion, up NOK 3.9 billion vs Q2
 2026, following the removal of the 15% discount and the roll-forward of the
 valuation basis to 2026 and 2027 figures. Adevinta continues to perform well,
 with H1 2026 revenues up 11% and adjusted EBITDA up 22% YoY, and an adjusted
 EBITDA margin of 50%.

title: KCC: Third Quarter 2026   Solid Q3, record Q4 outlook
body:
Oslo, 27 October 2026: Klaveness Combination Carriers ASA ("KCC") delivered
one of its strongest quarters in its history in Q3 2026, reporting EBITDA of
USD 40.4 million and Profit after tax of USD 23.6 million.
CEO Engebret Dahm commented: "KCC delivered another solid quarter, supported
by strong markets, improved trading efficiency and a higher number of earning
days following the delivery of our third and final CABU newbuilding. We enter
the fourth quarter with record-high TCE earnings guidance, underpinned by a
buoyant tanker market and solid dry bulk earnings. While geopolitical
disruption continues to drive market volatility, we remain focused on further
strengthening the resilience of our business."
KCC owns and operates a fleet of 19 combination carriers built for the
transportation of both wet and dry bulk cargoes. The vessels are operated in
trades where they efficiently combine dry and wet cargoes with minimum
ballast, capitalizing on imbalances in global trade flows.
Highlights for Third Quarter 2026:
* EBITDA of USD 40.4 million (Q2 2026: USD 38.5 million) and Profit after tax
 of USD 23.6 million (Q2 2026: USD 20.8 million)
* Fleet TCE earnings [1] of $36,116/day (Q2 2026: $37,782/day)
* Q3 2026 dividend of USD 0.36 per share, totaling approximately USD 21.4
 million (Q2 2026: USD 0.30 per share)
* More earning days from newbuilding deliveries and limited dry-docking
* Record-high Q4 TCE earnings guidance, with 64% of capacity fixed
The 5% increase in EBITDA and the 14% increase in profit after tax from Q2 to
Q3 2026 were mainly driven by a higher number of earning days following the
delivery of all three CABU newbuildings and less dry-docking off-hire.
The Board of Directors declares a quarterly dividend of USD 0.36 per share
(USD 21.4 million), an increase of 20% from last quarter.
With all 19 vessels in operation, limited dry-docking activity ahead and
exceptionally strong product tanker markets, KCC is set to deliver a record
quarterly result in Q4. Based on current fixed days equal to 74% of fleet
capacity for the CABU fleet, 50% of fleet capacity fixed for the CLEANBU fleet
and KCC's best estimates for open days, Q4 2026 TCE earnings guidance for the
CABU fleet is $43,000 - 48,000 $/day and 57,000 -- 67,000 $/day for the
CLEANBU fleet. Annual contract negotiations are ongoing, and KCC expects to
conclude 2026 with a solid contract book, further strengthening the Company's
resilience amid medium-term market uncertainty.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[1] TCE earnings $/day is an alternative performance measure (APM) defined and
reconciled in the excel sheet published together with the Company's Q3 2026
report on the Investor Relations section of www.combinationcarriers.com
(https://www.combinationcarriers.com/).
[2] Estimate based on booked cargoes and expected employment and rate for open
days.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

title: Salmon Evolution ASA: Fully focused on execution
body:
Salmon Evolution's (OSE: SALME) near-term priorities are to deliver Phase 1
and Phase 2 production targets and convert higher production into lower unit
costs. The company guides for 11,000-12,000 tonnes HOG harvested in 2027 and
targets run-rate farming EBITDA costs of NOK 60-65/kg by mid-2027.
In the third quarter of 2026 operations remained stable, with net biomass
growth of 1,984 tonnes LW. Phase 1 biomass growth was impacted by one
underperforming fish group, which was fully harvested during the quarter,
while Phase 2 growth continued according to plan.
"We remain fully focused on unlocking the Phase 1 biomass growth potential
through targeted and ongoing initiatives centered on continued water quality
improvements", said Salmon Evolution CEO Trond Håkon Schaug-Pettersen.
Salmon Evolution harvested 1,597 tonnes HOG in the third quarter, achieving an
all-in price realization of approximately NOK 64/kg and a superior share of
94%. Farming EBITDA was NOK -13.3 million, while Group EBITDA was NOK -20.2
million.
"Strong underlying demand and limited supply growth provide a favorable
backdrop for salmon prices as we move into 2027. With our production volumes
set to more than double next year, this provides a strong foundation for
Salmon Evolution as we enter the most exciting phase in the company's
history", said Salmon Evolution CEO Trond Håkon Schaug-Pettersen.
The 2026 harvest guidance is updated to approximately 5,500 tonnes HOG,
primarily reflecting the decision to move the first Phase 2 harvest using
available flexibility in the production plan.
Phase 2 ramp-up is progressing according to plan. Construction is expected to
finish by year-end, with formal handover of the final two tanks following
testing and commissioning in Q1 2027.
New credit facility:
Salmon Evolution has entered into a credit facility of up to NOK 200 million
with DNB Bank ASA. The purpose of the new facility is to provide the Company
with additional funding following lower-than-expected salmon prices.
The facility matures on 30 June 2027 and has a margin of NIBOR plus 500 bps,
including 50 bps in quarterly step-up. The Company will continue to evaluate
its financing and capital structure and consider available funding sources.
The loan agreement has been duly executed and closing of the facility has been
completed.
Results presentation:
CEO Trond Håkon Schaug-Pettersen and CFO Trond Vadset Veibust will present the
results for the third quarter 2026 at Hotel Continental in Oslo, Norway,
Wednesday 28 October at 08:00 CET.
The presentation and Q&A will be held in English, and participants may also
follow the presentation and submit questions through a live webcast available
on www.salmonevolution.no (http://www.salmonevolution.no/) or with the

title: Wallenius Wilhelmsen extends fleet renewal program
Delivering through disciplined execution
body:
In the third quarter, Telenor strengthened its operational momentum, delivering group service revenue growth of 1.6% and EBITDA growth of 1.5%. Free cash flow before M&A was strong, coming in at NOK 4.7 billion. KNL's defence framework agreement strengthened Telenor's foothold in the strategically important defence market, where demand for secure and resilient communications is growing.
Third quarter highlights:
- Service revenues of NOK 14.8 billion.
- Adjusted EBITDA of NOK 8.8 billion.
- Free cash flow before M&A of NOK 4.7 billion.
- Total free cash flow of NOK 8.5 billion.
Strong free cash flow 
Norway showed clear quarter-on-quarter improvement, supported by disciplined cost management. Sweden maintained its strong performance with its 15th consecutive quarter of EBITDA growth and 35,000 new mobile customers in the quarter. The sequential development in Finland and Denmark was stable. In Asia, Grameenphone also demonstrated cost discipline, maintaining profitability while returning to service revenue growth.
Net income attributable to shareholders of Telenor was NOK 9.8 billion, and adjusted earnings per share increased by 45% to NOK 2.70.
"With a strong financial position and modest leverage, we aim to accelerate the share buyback programme and complete the NOK 15 billion programme in two years rather than three," says President & CEO Benedicte Schilbred Fasmer.
Strengthened Nordic position within defence and broadband
During the quarter, Telenor's subsidiary KNL strengthened its position in secure defence communications by securing a framework agreement enabling the Danish Armed Forces to procure KNL's ultra-secure high-frequency communication systems. Denmark becomes the third Nordic country to join KNL's NORDEFCO agreement, alongside Finland and Sweden, further strengthening Nordic cooperation around secure and resilient communications.
"In today's security environment, secure and resilient communications are more critical than ever. KNL's presence across the Nordic defence sector reflects the increasing demand for trusted and independent solutions and strengthens Telenor's position in mission-critical communications," says Schilbred Fasmer.
Telenor is also strengthening the position within broadband in Norway and Sweden.
"With the acquisition of Bahnhof in the third quarter, we are further expanding our Nordic broadband footprint, building on the previously announced GlobalConnect and Enivest transactions. Together, these transactions will add more than 650,000 consumer broadband relationships and strengthen our competitive positions in both Norway and Sweden," says Schilbred Fasmer.
AI increases the speed and scale of digital attacks 
Telenor's 2026 Security Report shows how artificial intelligence is accelerating digital attacks. AI enables attackers to find vulnerabilities faster, automate known attack methods and target far more companies at the same time.
"AI is changing the rules of the game for digital security. This gives us less time to respond and raises the bar for preparedness and cooperation between businesses and public authorities," says Schilbred Fasmer.
Geopolitics, security, and emergency preparedness were also central themes in the very first Telenor Conference, which brought together business leaders, politicians, and media in Oslo last week.
Financial outlook for 2026:
We reaffirm our full year outlook and our longer-term ambitions remain unchanged:
Telenor Group
- Flat to slightly negative organic growth in adjusted EBITDA.
- Free cash flow before M&A excluding dividends from associated companies and incremental spectrum of around NOK 10 billion.
Nordic telcos
- Flat to low-single-digit organic growth in service revenues.
- Flat to low-single-digit organic growth in adjusted EBITDA.
- Around 14% capex to sales (excluding leases).
As usual, the outlook excludes potential items related to prior years' activities, including Telenor Norway's TV VAT provision for 2020-2022 of NOK 0.2 billion.

title: Målrettet gjennomføring gir resultater
body:
I tredje kvartal styrket Telenor den operasjonelle utviklingen med vekst i tjenesteinntekter og EBITDA på henholdsvis 1,6 og 1,5 prosent. Fri kontantstrøm før M&A var sterk og endte på 4,7 milliarder kroner. KNL sin rammeavtale innen forsvar styrket Telenors posisjon i det strategisk viktige forsvarsmarkedet, der etterspørselen etter sikker og robust kommunikasjon er økende.
Høydepunkter i tredje kvartal
- Tjenesteinntekter på 14,8 milliarder kroner.
- Justert EBITDA på 8,8 milliarder kroner.
- Fri kontantstrøm før M&A på 4,7 milliarder kroner.
- Total fri kontantstrøm på 8,5 milliarder kroner.
Sterk fri kontantstrøm
Norge viste tydelig forbedring fra forrige kvartal, drevet av god kostnadsdisiplin. Sverige fortsatte den sterke utviklingen og leverte sitt 15. kvartal på rad med EBITDA-vekst, i tillegg til 35 000 nye mobilkunder i kvartalet. Utviklingen fra forrige kvartal i Finland og Danmark var stabil. I Asia opprettholdt Grameenphone lønnsomheten gjennom god kostnadskontroll, samtidig som selskapet igjen kunne vise til vekst i tjenesteinntektene.
Resultat etter skatt henført til aksjonærene i Telenor var 9,8 milliarder kroner, og justert resultat per aksje økte med 45 prosent til 2,70 kroner.
- Med en sterk finansiell posisjon og beskjeden gjeldsgrad har vi som mål å fremskynde aksjetilbakekjøpsprogrammet og fullføre 15 milliarder kroner i tilbakekjøp på to år i stedet for tre, sier konsernsjef Schilbred Fasmer. 
Styrket nordisk posisjon innen forsvar og bredbånd
I løpet av kvartalet styrket Telenors datterselskap KNL sin posisjon innen sikker forsvarskommunikasjon gjennom en rammeavtale som gjør det mulig for det danske forsvaret å anskaffe KNLs ultrasikre kommunikasjonssystemer for HF-kommunikasjon. Danmark blir dermed det tredje nordiske landet som tiltrer KNLs NORDEFCO-avtale, sammen med Finland og Sverige. Avtalen bidrar til å styrke det nordiske samarbeidet om sikker og robust kommunikasjon.
- I dagens sikkerhetssituasjon er sikker og robust kommunikasjon viktigere enn noen gang. KNLs posisjon i det nordiske forsvarsmarkedet viser den økende etterspørselen etter sikre og uavhengige kommunikasjonsløsninger, og styrker Telenors posisjon innen samfunnskritisk kommunikasjon, sier konsernsjef Benedicte Schilbred Fasmer.
Telenor styrker også sin posisjon innen bredbånd i Norge og Sverige.
- Med oppkjøpet av Bahnhof i tredje kvartal utvider vi vår nordiske bredbåndsvirksomhet ytterligere, i forlengelsen av de tidligere annonserte transaksjonene med GlobalConnect og Enivest. Samlet vil disse transaksjonene tilføre mer enn 650 000 bredbåndskundeforhold i privatmarkedet og styrke våre konkurranseposisjoner i både Norge og Sverige, sier Schilbred Fasmer.
KI øker farten og omfanget av digitale angrep
Telenors sikkerhetsrapport for 2026 viser hvordan kunstig intelligens øker tempoet i digitale angrep. KI gjør det mulig for angripere å finne sårbarheter raskere, automatisere kjente angrepsmetoder og rette angrep mot langt flere virksomheter samtidig.
- KI endrer spillereglene for digital sikkerhet. Det gir oss kortere tid til å reagere og stiller nye krav til beredskap og samarbeid mellom næringslivet og myndighetene, sier Schilbred Fasmer.
Geopolitikk, sikkerhet og beredskap sto også sentralt under den aller første Telenorkonferansen, som samlet næringslivsledere, politikere og mediene i Oslo forrige uke.
Finansielle utsikter for 2026
Vi opprettholder utsiktene for 2026, og våre langsiktige ambisjoner ligger fast:
Telenor-konsernet
- Flat til svakt negativ organisk vekst i justert EBITDA. 
- Fri kontantstrøm før M&A, eksklusive utbytte fra tilknyttede selskaper og inkrementelle spektrumkostnader, på rundt 10 milliarder kroner.
Nordiske teleselskaper
- Flat til lav ensifret organisk vekst i tjenesteinntekter.
- Flat til lav ensifret organisk vekst i justert EBITDA.
- Driftsinvesteringer på rundt 14 prosent av inntektene, eksklusive leieavtaler.
Som vanlig er eventuelle poster knyttet til tidligere års virksomhet holdt utenfor utsiktene, herunder Telenor Norges avsetning for MVA på TV-tjenester for 2020-2022 på 0,2 milliarder kroner.

title: Norwegian Group with strong third quarter results
body:
The Norwegian Group today reports an operating result of NOK 2,728 million for the third quarter of 2026. The figures demonstrate the group's ability to deliver strong financial results underpinned by a focus on cost control and robust operational performance in the busiest travel season of the year.
For the third quarter of 2026, Norwegian Group delivered an operating result (EBIT) of NOK 2,728 million, corresponding to an operating margin of 21.4 percent. Profit before tax (EBT) amounted to NOK 2,520 million for the quarter. The liquidity position was NOK 11.2 billion at quarter-end, up NOK 0.7 billion from the end of the third quarter of 2025, after the final repayment of the company's last outstanding bond in September.
"The third quarter was characterised by strong operational performance across the group during the peak summer travel season and a continued focus on cost control. Widerøe continues to uphold world class punctuality, now five months in a row, and was highlighted by Cirium in July. Norwegian was named among Europe's top five punctual airlines in both August and September. This highlights the great work across both airlines with the continued focus on operational performance. While the current macroeconomic climate is uncertain, booking trends remain encouraging with the number of sold tickets significantly higher than at the same time last year," says Geir Karlsen, CEO of Norwegian.
The Norwegian Group had 8.75 million passengers in the third quarter, of which 7.64 million were passengers of Norwegian and 1.1 million of Widerøe. Capacity (ASK) for Norwegian increased by 5 percent in the third quarter, while Widerøe's capacity increased by 2 percent. The quarterly load factor for Norwegian was 88.5 percent, up 0.2 percentage points from the same period last year. For Widerøe, the quarterly load factor was 76.1 percent.
Punctuality, share of flights departing on schedule, showed solid improvements for both airlines. Punctuality improved to 80.7 percent for Norwegian, up 2.9 percentage points from last year, and to 93.5 percent for Widerøe, up 1.7 percentage points. Regularity was 99.3 percent and 97.9 percent, respectively, with regularity at both airlines negatively impacted by the air traffic controller strike in Norway in August. 
Norwegian Reward reaches milestone 
In September, Norwegian Reward introduced five new status levels, simplifying how frequent flyers track and earn benefits with Norwegian and Widerøe. The update unlocks tailored benefits for every level, supporting the award-winning loyalty programme as it surpassed 10 million members.
"Surpassing 10 million members in Norwegian Reward is a major milestone, and the introduction of five new status levels together with our joint loyalty platform Spenn further strengthens our offering across the Nordics," says Geir Karlsen, CEO of Norwegian.
Looking ahead into the upcoming winter season, Norwegian has reduced monthly capacity by between 25 and 40 percent compared to October 2026. Production for the winter season is forecasted to increase marginally compared to the same period last year.
The forecasted production (ASK) is for the full year of 2026, is 2 percent for both Norwegian and Widerøe. Norwegian is progressing well with its profitability initiatives under Program X, which are on track to deliver annual recurring underlying profit improvements more than NOK 1.25 billion by the end of 2026. Underlying unit cost excluding fuel for Norwegian is forecasted to remain unchanged in 2026 compared to 2025.
The Norwegian Group fleet comprised 148 aircraft at quarter-end, with 98 aircraft in the Norwegian fleet, including 39 latest-technology Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft following the delivery of three new aircraft during the quarter, and 50 in the Widerøe fleet.
The regulatory process for the acquisition of Nordic Leisure Travel Group (NLTG) is progressing as planned, and subject to EU competition clearance, the transaction is still targeted to close by year-end.

title: Aker Solutions ASA: Third-quarter results 2026
body:
October 28, 2026 - Aker Solutions continued to deliver solid financial results
in the third quarter of 2026. Several milestones have been met across the
project portfolio in the period. The company now expects 2026 revenue to be
between NOK 53 and 55 billion with an EBITDA margin between 7.5 and 8.0 percent
excluding net profit from SLB OneSubsea.
3Q 2026 Financial Highlights
(excluding special items)
 - Revenue NOK 13.5 billion
 - EBITDA NOK 1.3 billion
 - EBITDA margin 9.6 percent
 - Earnings per share NOK 1.45
 - Order intake NOK 5.4 billion (0.4x book-to-bill)
 - Order backlog NOK 69.3 billion
 - Net cash position NOK 5.8 billion, including investments in liquid funds
"During the quarter, we have met several important milestones in our project
portfolio. Combined with solid financial performance, this reflects the
expertise and dedication of our people", said Paal Eikeseth, Chief Executive
Officer of Aker Solutions.
"At the same time, we are transforming how we execute projects. By standardizing
solutions, moving from documents to data and applying decades of project
knowledge to AI-supported digital tools, we are building a more agile, efficient
and competitive Aker Solutions", said Eikeseth.
Key Developments
Revenue in the third quarter was NOK 13.5 billion, in line with expectations
following peak activity in 2025. Underlying EBITDA was NOK 1.3 billion and
EBITDA margin for the quarter was 9.6 percent, or 7.7 percent excluding net
profit from SLB OneSubsea. Order intake for the quarter was NOK 5.4 billion, and
the secured backlog at the end of the quarter stood at NOK 69.3 billion.
The net cash position increased to NOK 5.8 billion in the quarter, including
investments in liquid funds. Working capital improved by NOK 677 million, while
CAPEX was NOK 67 million. Aker Solutions received NOK 137 million in quarterly
dividends from SLB OneSubsea during the period.
Operationally, Aker Solutions met several important milestones in its project
portfolio, including the sail-away of Aker BP's Valhall PWP and Hugin B topside
platforms. In addition, the Life Cycle segment delivered strong operational
performance across their portfolio of frame agreements and modification
projects.
SLB OneSubsea, where Aker Solutions owns 20 percent, also delivered improved
financial results. Revenue was USD 1.1 billion, an increase of 12 percent
compared to the same period last year. The underlying EBITDA margin in the
quarter was 18.5 percent. SLB OneSubsea is on track to deliver on its order
intake ambitions, positioning the company for growth from 2027 onwards. Based on
its robust financial position, SLB OneSubsea is expected to distribute dividends
of around USD 400 million to its shareholders in 2026, in line with full-year
distribution in 2025.
Outlook and Guidance
Aker Solutions expects full-year 2026 revenue to be between NOK 53 and 55
billion, with an EBITDA margin between 7.5 and 8.0 percent excluding net profit
from SLB OneSubsea.
For 2027, Aker Solutions expects revenue to decline to between NOK 35 and 40
billion, with an EBITDA margin between 7.0 and 8.0 percent excluding net profit
from SLB OneSubsea.
Aker Solutions is taking action to reshape the business, reduce the cost base
and align capacity with the lower activity expected in 2027, while improving
competitiveness.

title: BlueNord Announces Third Quarter of 2026 Results
body:
Oslo, 28 2026: BlueNord ASA ("BlueNord" or the "Company") has today announced
its financial results for the third quarter of 2026, reflecting an overall
strong performance both operationally and financially, mainly driven by higher
production and favourable commodity prices.
Highlights:
 - Net hydrocarbon production of 43.6 mboepd with Tyra reaching peak production
levels of c. 30mboepd during the quarter and stability improving significantly
 - Total revenues of USD 346 million in the third quarter, up from USD 276.8
million in the previous quarter
 - EBITDA of USD 219.6 million in Q3 compared to USD 146.8 million in Q2
 - Available liquidity of USD 392.8 million, with cash on balance sheet of USD
131.3 million and undrawn RBL capacity of USD 261 million
 - Proposed statutory merger with Vår Energi ASA announced and approved by
shareholders
Operational
BlueNord delivered a total net production of 43.6 mboepd in the third quarter of
2026, reflecting the successfully planned maintenance shutdowns at both the Tyra
and Gorm hubs earlier in the summer. The Tyra hub significantly improved its
stability and capacity after the planned June shutdown. A step change in
production was observed with gas production around export capacity, and
production reaching c. 30 mboepd during the quarter.
Financials
Revenue for the quarter was USD 346 million, primarily driven by higher oil and
gas sales volumes and increased commodity prices, partly offset by a higher
hedge effect. EBITDA was USD 219.6 million, with net operating cash flow of USD
69.7 million (USD 212 million before working capital and tax payments). During
the quarter, the BNOR18 bonds were listed on Oslo Stock Exchange.
Transaction with Vår Energi
On 21 July 2026, Vår Energi ASA and BlueNord ASA announced a proposed statutory
merger of which Vår Energi's 100% owned subsidiary is the surviving entity. The
proposed merger and merger plan was approved by BlueNord's shareholders at an
Extraordinary General Meeting on 24 August 2026. BlueNord shareholders will
receive 9.7153 newly issued shares in Vår Energi and NOK 76.83 in cash per
share. BlueNord's shareholders will also be compensated for dividends in Vår
Energi declared before the merger completion, in accordance with the merger
plan. Closing of the transaction is expected around the year-end 2026, subject
to several conditions' precedent, including regulatory and governmental
approvals as outlined in the merger plan.
"Our shareholders approved the merger with Vår Energi in August, and BlueNord is
now approaching the end of its journey as an independent company. We can look
back on it with real satisfaction. Since we acquired our interest in the DUC in
2019, Tyra has been redeveloped and brought back into production, and we have
returned substantial cash to our shareholders.
Our success as a standalone company provides a strong foundation for BlueNord's
next chapter. As part of Vår Energi, we believe our shareholders will benefit
from greater scale and diversification while continuing our shared commitment to
maximising operational performance and delivering long-term returns. The
combination offers an opportunity to build on what both companies have achieved
independently, and we are working through the remaining steps to completion. We
expect the merger to close around the end of the year.
This quarter Tyra delivered a step change in performance. Following the planned
maintenance campaign in June we saw record production days close to 30 mboepd
and gas export at maximum capacity. Until completion our focus is unchanged:
running the business well and working to complete the transaction.
Finally, I want to thank everyone at BlueNord for what they have delivered, and
our shareholders for their support," said Euan Shirlaw, Chief Executive Officer
of BlueNord.

title: Borregaard ASA: All-time high EBITDA1 of NOK 557 million in the 3rd quarter
body:
Borregaard's operating revenues increased to NOK 1,894 million (NOK 1,799
million) in the 3(rd) quarter of 2026. EBITDA(1) reached an all-time high of NOK
557 million (NOK 440 million). The results in all areas increased compared with
the 3(rd) quarter of 2025.
In BioSolutions, selective price increases and reduced costs were the main
reasons for the improved result. Higher deliveries and strong production were
the main reasons for an all-time high result in BioMaterials. In Fine Chemicals,
the result improved due to higher deliveries of both fine chemical intermediates
and bioethanol. Savings from the ongoing cost improvement programme and energy
system optimisation contributed positively to the Group's results in the
quarter. Net currency effects were positive for the Group.
Profit before tax was NOK 394 million (NOK 247 million). Earnings per share were
NOK 2.96 (NOK 1.96).
"Borregaard delivered an all-time high quarterly EBITDA with higher results
across all business areas, strong operational performance at the Sarpsborg
biorefinery, savings from the cost improvement programme, optimisation of our
energy system, and selective price increases", says CEO Tom Erik Foss-Jacobsen.

Our success as a standalone company provides a strong foundation for BlueNord's
next chapter. As part of Vår Energi, we believe our shareholders will benefit
from greater scale and diversification while continuing our shared commitment to
maximising operational performance and delivering long-term returns. The
combination offers an opportunity to build on what both companies have achieved
independently, and we are working through the remaining steps to completion. We
expect the merger to close around the end of the year.
This quarter Tyra delivered a step change in performance. Following the planned
maintenance campaign in June we saw record production days close to 30 mboepd
and gas export at maximum capacity. Until completion our focus is unchanged:
running the business well and working to complete the transaction.
Finally, I want to thank everyone at BlueNord for what they have delivered, and
our shareholders for their support," said Euan Shirlaw, Chief Executive Officer
of BlueNord.

title: Circio delivers three presentations at ESGCT and shows novel AAV circVec 5.2 design for enhanced heart expression and specificity
body:
* New heart-optimized circVec 5.2 design shows approximately 200-fold higher
 gene expression compared to conventional AAV vectors, with 95% cardiac
 specificity and less than 1% off-target expression in liver
* The competitive oral presentation at ESGCT follows the ASCGT presentation in
 May, marking back-to-back selections at the two leading global gene and cell
 therapy conferences
* In the oral presentation, Circio is showcasing the versatile circVec
 circular RNA gene expression platform, with a focus on non-viral vectors for
 in vivo cell therapy applications
* Two posters demonstrate the potential of circVec to enhance gene expression
 and specificity across heart, eye and CNS, supporting the development of
 more effective and safer gene therapies
Oslo, Norway, 28 October 2026 -- Circio Holding ASA (OSE: CRNA), a
biotechnology company developing novel circular RNA expression technology for
gene and cell therapy, today announces the materials for its oral and two
poster presentations that are being delivered at the 33rd Annual Congress of
the European Society of Gene and Cell Therapy (ESGCT) in Hamburg, Germany.
In the oral presentation, Circio s CTO Dr. Thomas B Hansen presents the latest
developments for its circVec platform and its potential for in vivo CAR-T
therapy, an area attracting significant momentum in the life sciences
industry. Circio s approach formulates circVec DNA constructs into LNP
particles with the aim to establish a novel technology platform for potent,
durable and immune-quiet CAR expression in T-cells. This unique combination
could establish a new in vivo therapeutic window for cancer and autoimmunity,
bridging the gap between transient, short-lived RNA-based approaches and
permanently integrating, irreversible lentiviral systems.
"Presenting the evolution of the circVec technology from the first to the
fifth generation in an oral session at ESGCT is an excellent opportunity to
show how far the platform has come and its range of therapeutic applications,"
said Dr. Thomas B Hansen, CTO of Circio. "Across heart, eye and CNS, circVec
delivers strong, specific and consistent expression gains over conventional
AAV gene therapy, driven by the superior stability of circular RNA. The broad
and robust performance makes circVec a platform technology that can be applied
across different vectors, tissues and diseases. With each new generation we
have further improved both potency and precision, and we see substantial
potential for circVec as an integral component of next generation gene and
cell therapies."
The two posters highlight the potential of circVec to improve the potency and
specificity of AAV vectors to support the development of more effective next
generation gene therapies. circVec 3.2 and 4.0 show up to approximately 40-,
50- and 60-fold increased expression in heart, eye and CNS, respectively. The
new heart-optimised AAV9 circVec 5.2 design further enhances potency and
cardiac specificity, achieving approximately 200-fold higher gene expression
than conventional mRNA-based AAV9. Importantly, circVec 5.2 shows 95%
heart-specific expression, compared with 25% for conventional mRNA-based AAV9,
while reducing off-target liver expression to less than 1%, compared with 9%
for conventional AAV9. These results highlight the ability of circVec to
enhance on-target tissue activity while minimizing unwanted payload expression
in off-target tissues, an important feature for enabling more specific gene
therapies and reducing toxicity.
"Being selected for a competitive oral presentation at both the ASGCT and
ESGCT 2026 annual meetings reflects the growing recognition of Circio in the
gene and cell therapy field," said Dr. Erik D Wiklund, CEO of Circio.
"Following the new and enhanced circVec 5.2 design and validation in vivo,
Circio is advancing its pre-clinical cardiac program. This is an area where
circVec really stands out, with strong potential to offer enhanced and safer
gene therapies for patients with high and urgent medical needs. With the USD
88 million in new funding secured during 2026, Circio is now rapidly
progressing into in vivo heart disease models to confirm the potential of
AAV-circVec in therapeutic systems. Studies are starting in first quarter
2027, and we can look forward to several important read-outs during the year."

Biogenesis for Next-Generation T Cell Therapies

heart and eye that are expected to complete during November.

title: Scatec secures financing for the first phase of the Dandara solar and BESS project in Egypt
body:
Oslo/Cairo, 28 October 2026: Scatec ASA ("Scatec"), a leading renewable energy
solutions provider, has signed loan agreements for the first phase of the
Dandara (Egypt Aluminium) project in Egypt and is starting construction of the
power plant. Scatec has further signed a partnership agreement with National
Bank of Egypt (NBE), which will join with a 20% ownership stake in the
project.
The first phase of the project comprises a 569 MW solar plant and a 100-MWh
battery energy storage system, supplying renewable electricity to Egypt
Aluminium under a 25-year power purchase agreement which is backed by a
sovereign guarantee. Dandara will generate approximately 1.4 TWh of clean
electricity and lead to abatement of more than 550,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions
annually, helping Egypt Aluminium reduce its carbon footprint and meet
evolving trade-related environmental standards, and strengthen the appeal and
competitiveness of Egyptian products in international markets.
The non-recourse project financing comprises USD 217 million and is provided
by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), African
Development Bank (AfDB), and European Investment Bank (EIB). The financing
amount corresponds to approximately 80% of total estimated capex for the first
phase of USD 271 million.
Following the NBE and recently announced EBRD transactions, Scatec holds a 56%
ownership interest in the Dandara project; 36% through the EBRD platform and
20% outside the platform. Scatec intends to invite additional equity partners
into the project and secure equity bridge loans (EBLs), allowing its equity
injection to be deferred until the end of the construction period.
Scatec will deliver Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC), Asset
Management (AM), and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) services for the project.
Scatec's EPC scope is approximately 80% of total capex. Commercial operation
for the first phase is targeted in the first half of 2028. Scatec expects to
commence construction of the second phase in H1 2027.
"Dandara is another major milestone in Scatec's journey in Egypt. Building on
the successful delivery of Obelisk, Africa's largest hybrid solar and battery
installation, we are now bringing the same integrated model to industrial
decarbonisation at scale. Supplying renewable power to one of Egypt's most
energy-intensive industries under a long-term agreement backed by a sovereign
guarantee demonstrate the quality of what we are building in Egypt, and the
confidence that leading development finance institutions place in Scatec as a
partner. Egypt is one of our most important markets, and Dandara reinforces
our position as a long-term contributor to the country's energy transition,"
says Scatec CEO Terje Pilskog.

title: Third quarter 2026 results
body:
Aker BP delivered strong earnings and cash flow in the third quarter, driven by
efficient operations, higher sold volumes and strong realised prices. The
Yggdrasil and Valhall PWP-Fenris projects passed major offshore milestones and
remain on track for first production next summer, while the Skarv Satellites
Project came on stream in late August.
Highlights
 - Production: Net production was 374 mboepd, reflecting planned maintenance.
Full-year production guidance of 380-400 mboepd is reiterated.
 - Sales: Net sold volumes were 396 mboepd, up five percent from the previous
quarter.
 - Earnings and cash flow: EBITDA was USD 3.4 billion, and cash flow from
operations was USD 2.4 billion.
 - Net profit: USD 986 million, equivalent to USD 1.56 per share, including a
positive after-tax effect of USD 262 million from an impairment reversal.
 - Projects: Yggdrasil and Valhall PWP-Fenris progressed according to plan. The
Hugin B, Munin and Valhall PWP topsides were installed, all major subsea
components at Yggdrasil are now in place, and offshore hook-up and commissioning
are underway.
 - Skarv Satellites: Production commenced in late August, almost a year ahead
of the original schedule.
 - Financial position: The financial position remained robust, with a leverage
ratio of 0.50 and USD 5.8 billion in available liquidity.
 - Dividend: A quarterly dividend of USD 0.6615 per share is payable on or
about 12 November 2026.
Commenting on the results, CEO Karl Johnny Hersvik said:
"Aker BP delivered strong results in the third quarter, supported by safe and
reliable operations, higher sold volumes and strong realised prices. Our
financial position remains robust, with low leverage and substantial liquidity."
"Offshore, this was one of the most important quarters in our project history.
With the Hugin B, Munin and Valhall PWP topsides installed and all major subsea
components in place at Yggdrasil, we have entered the final phase towards start
-up of both Yggdrasil and Valhall PWP-Fenris next summer. I am particularly
pleased that the Skarv Satellites Project came on stream almost a year ahead of
the original schedule. This demonstrates our execution capabilities and the
value of developing new resources through existing infrastructure."
"As we look beyond the current project portfolio, we see substantial
opportunities for continued value creation on the Norwegian Continental Shelf.
We are strengthening our opportunity set through exploration and new
partnerships, while using technology, AI and a more integrated operating model
to unlock more resources and improve how we work. Our strategy remains
unchanged, but we are improving how we execute it to create even more
shareholder value."

The presentation will be webcast today at 08:30 CEST on
www.akerbp.com (https://www.akerbp.com/en), hosted by CEO Karl Johnny Hersvik
and CFO David Tønne. The presentation will be followed by an online Q&A session.

title: Smartoptics Group ASA (SMOP) - Q3 2026 Financial Results
body:
Oslo, Norway - October 29, 2026 - Smartoptics Group ASA (Smartoptics, OSE: SMOP)
today reported the strongest quarter in the company's history, with revenue
increasing 80 percent year-on-year to USD 34.3 million and EBIT margin improving
by 12 percentage points to 20.6 percent. Gross margin was 49.5 percent, in line
with the same period in 2025.
The growth was broad-based, with all-time high revenue in all regions. Solutions
revenue more than doubled, driven by large account deliveries, while Software &
Services grew 69 percent. With revenue of approximately USD 109 million over the
last four quarters, Smartoptics has now passed the USD 100 million target set at
the listing in 2021.
"The third quarter was the strongest in Smartoptics' history. Revenue grew 80
percent and EBIT grew by 340% to USD 7.1 million," said Magnus Grenfeldt, CEO of
Smartoptics, and continued:
"We see clear evidence of the operating leverage in our model, as revenue grows
faster than our cost base while we continue to invest in future growth. Our
large account strategy continues to deliver. Repeat customers have grown
significantly, and we are now engaging with even larger players, laying the
foundation for the next step towards our financial aspirations."
Revenue in the Americas grew 86 percent to USD 20.2 million, EMEA grew 72
percent to USD 10.6 million, and APAC grew 75 percent to USD 3.6 million.
Operating cash flow was strong at USD 7.6 million.
The market backdrop remains highly supportive. Investment in AI infrastructure
is increasing the demand for optical networking, while demand for bandwidth
extends well beyond AI, across data center interconnect, network modernization,
broadband, financial services and other areas. Smartoptics' mid-term financial
aspirations remain unchanged: revenue of USD 300-400 million and beyond over
time, corresponding to average annual growth exceeding 25 percent from 2026, and
an EBIT margin above 16 percent in the second half of the planning period.
"What got us here will take us further. We have broadened our hardware and
software offering and our addressable market, built stronger processes and our
strongest team ever, while preserving the challenger culture that keeps us
nimble. With a proven playbook, a substantially larger market and strong
momentum, we believe Smartoptics is well positioned for the next phase of
growth," said Grenfeldt.
The report and presentation for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026
are enclosed.

About Smartoptics
Smartoptics provides innovative optical networking solutions and devices for the
new era of open networking. Our customer base includes thousands of enterprises,
governments, cloud providers, Internet exchanges as well as cable and telecom
operators. We have an open networking approach in everything we do which allows
our customers to break unwanted vendor lock-in, remain flexible and minimize

increasingly rely on data center services and specifications. Smartoptics is a
