title: Bygger fundamentet for en sterk, nasjonal sparebank
body:
Sparebanken Norge har i tredje kvartal 2026 et resultat før skatt på 2.138 millioner kroner. Egenkapitalavkastningen er 12,7 prosent, mens egenkapitalavkastning justert for fusjonseffekter (ROTE) utgjør 14,5 prosent i kvartalet. Hittil i år er egenkapitalavkastningen 14,2 %, mens egenkapitalavkastning justert for fusjonseffekter utgjør 16,2 %. 
Sterk utlånsvekst i bedrifts- og personmarkedet
Brutto utlån til kunder utgjør 513,2 milliarder kroner ved utgangen av kvartalet. Utlån til personkunder økte med 1,4 prosent i kvartalet, mens utlån til bedriftskunder økte med 2,2 prosent. 
Banken er i rute med etableringen i nye markedsområder, og har i kvartalet fullført viktige ansettelser av rådgivere og ledere. I løpet av de neste 12 månedene skal Sparebanken Norge være på plass ytterligere to steder: Mo i Rana og Trondheim.
- Vi leverer nok et kvartal med god utlånsvekst. Innenfor både personmarked og bedriftsmarked er veksten god, og et resultat av strukturert arbeid over tid. Samtidig ser vi at de nye markedsområder begynner å levere vekst, hvilket lover godt for den vekstreisen banken nå er på, sier konsernsjef Jan Erik Kjerpeseth.
God kostnadskontroll til tross for fusjonskostnader og investering i nye markedsområder
Driftskostnader i prosent av netto driftsinntekter er 31,8 (29,4) % i kvartalet, og 31,8 (28,4) % hittil i år. Korrigert for sammenslåingskostnader ville kostnadsprosenten hittil i år vært om lag 31,0 %.
- Vi utviser god kostnadskontroll i 2026, i et år som preges av betydelige fusjonskostnader og begrenset effekt av kostnadssynergier. Den vellykkede tekniske fusjonen som ble gjennomført i oktober 2026, samt bemanningstilpasningen, vil øke synergitakten vesentlig inn i 2027, sier Kjerpeseth.
Sterk kapitalposisjon gir rom for både vekst og utbytte fremover 
Ren kjernekapitaldekning er 18,1 (18,1) % ved utgangen av kvartalet. Ved utgangen av kvartalet har banken en margin til soliditetsmålet på om lag 2,2 prosentpoeng.
- Vi er en godt kapitalisert bank, med en konservativ lånebok med lav risiko. Vi skal over tid være kapitaleffektive, og har akkurat nå rom for både å realisere ambisiøse vekstmål og tilby konkurransedyktige utbytter, sier Kjerpeseth. 
Hovedpunkter tredje kvartal 2026 
- Egenkapitalavkastning på 12,7 (14,5) prosent
- Netto renteinntekter på 2.664 (2.760) millioner kroner
- Netto provisjonsinntekter på 493 (452) millioner
- Kostnadsprosent 31,8 (29,4) prosent til tross for at sammenslåingskostnader utgjør om lag 26 millioner kroner
- Nedskrivninger på utlån og garantier på 97 (73) millioner kroner 
- Resultat pr. egenkapitalbevis er 3,66 (4,01) kroner
- Ren kjernekapitaldekning på 18,1 (18,1) prosent, godt over soliditetsmålet på 15,9 prosent

Siden 1823 har vi opparbeidet oss tillit hos kundene, som gjør at vi har en solid markedsposisjon. 
Gjennom våre tilknyttede produktselskaper er vi et komplett finanshus for alle våre person- og bedriftskunder. Vi er stolte over å være et selvstendig finanskonsern med hovedkontorer i Bergen og Kristiansand, med en sentral rolle i mye av den verdiskapningen som skjer i landet.

title: Kongsberg Maritime Q3 2026: Record-high order backlog and solid execution
body:
Kongsberg Maritime ASA (OSE: KMAR) today announced its results for the third
quarter 2026. Strong newbuild demand contributed to increased order intake and
a record order backlog.
Order intake reached MNOK 8,323 in the quarter, corresponding to a
book-to-bill ratio of 1.25. The order backlog increased to MNOK 29,753,
providing a solid foundation. Revenues were MNOK 6,639, which is 5% higher
than Q3 last year. Deliveries to newbuilds grew 16% while the aftermarket
declined by 5%.
EBITDA came in at MNOK 1,041, corresponding to an EBITDA margin of 15.7%.
EBITDA was impacted by MNOK 72 in restructuring costs related to the ongoing
competitiveness improvement program.
"The third-quarter result demonstrate our continued ability to scale
profitability on newbuild deliveries. Solid order intake across several vessel
segments further increased our record order backlog and supports our growth
ambitions for the coming years," says Lisa Edvardsen Haugan, President and CEO
of Kongsberg Maritime.
Key financial highlights Q3
* Order backlog: MNOK 29,753
* Revenues: MNOK 6,639
* EBITDA: MNOK 1,041
* EBITDA margin: 15.7%
* Order intake: MNOK 8,323
* Book-to-bill: 1.25
"2026 is shaping up to be a very strong year for shipyard orders for new
vessels. Our own contracting activity confirms that we are benefiting from
this," Edvardsen Haugan says.
Strong newbuild markets
Newbuild order intake remained strong with a book-to-bill of 1.39 in the third
quarter. Offshore Energy, Naval & Government and Cargo are representing the
largest vessel segments year-to-date. The broad distribution of orders across
segments provides balanced exposure to several long-term growth drivers.
The continued order momentum lifted the total backlog by MNOK 1,347 from the
second quarter, strengthening visibility for future deliveries.
"Our broad portfolio and deep domain knowledge allow us to support customers
across a wide range of vessel segments. Customers are increasingly looking for
integrated solutions that improve efficiency, reliability and vessel
performance. This, combined with our ability to support customers' operations
throughout the lifecycle of their vessels, is a key reason why we continue to
win significant newbuild contracts," says Edvardsen Haugan.
Berg Propulsion
Shortly after the end of the quarter, on 1 October, Kongsberg Maritime
completed the acquisition of the Swedish company Berg Propulsion AB,
strengthening its portfolio of propulsion and electrical systems.
Berg Propulsion complements Kongsberg Maritime's existing offering and expands
the company's ability to provide integrated propulsion solutions to a broader
range of customers and vessel segments. The business will be consolidated into
the Propulsion & Handling division.
Additional information
Kongsberg Maritime will present its results for the third quarter of 2026 on
Friday, 30 October, at 08:15 CET. The presentation will be streamed live at
www.kongsbergmaritime.com.
The report and presentation material will be published at
www.kongsbergmaritime.com and www.newsweb.no.
About Us
Kongsberg Maritime is a global leader in maritime technology. We deliver
advanced solutions for merchant, offshore, fishing and naval vessels, setting
new standards for safe, efficient and sustainable operations, both for
newbuilds and existing fleets. In close collaboration with customers and
research environments, we develop technology that solves real challenges at
sea. Today, more than 30,000 vessels operate with our systems on board.
Kongsberg Maritime has 8,800 employees in 35 countries.

title: Scatec third quarter 2026: Doubling growth pace, fully self-funded
body:
Oslo, 30 October 2026: In the third quarter, Scatec continued to progress its
near-term growth portfolio. Proportionate revenues were NOK 2,267 million
(2,953 million), and EBITDA was NOK 1,208 million (1,063 million).
Power production revenues were NOK 1,301 million (1,178 million) and EBITDA
NOK 1,070 million (955 million). The growth is driven by new power plants in
operation. Total proportionate power production from Scatec's power plants was
1,469 GWh (1,202 GWh).
The Development & Construction (D&C) segment reported revenues of NOK 948
million (1,760 million) and EBITDA of NOK 168 million (135 million). Revenues
in the same quarter last year were mainly driven by high activity on the
Obelisk project. The strong EBITDA margin this quarter was positively impacted
by NOK 140 million in close-out effects related to the Obelisk project,
including a contingency release of NOK 100 million. Total contingency releases
in 2026 amount to NOK 340 million.
"In the third quarter, we continued to deliver on our growth strategy, with
high construction activity, new assets increasing production by 22% and
several important milestones reached. We are also facing challenges in some
markets. In Ukraine, attacks on energy infrastructure continue to disrupt
operations, with employee safety our priority. In the Philippines, the
suspension of the reserves market will affect near-term earnings, but demand
for ancillary services remains strong and we expect a limited long-term
impact," says Scatec CEO Terje Pilskog.
Scatec has reached several important milestones since last reporting:
* Started construction of two new projects: the 900 MW Shadwan project in
 Egypt, one of Africa's largest onshore wind power plants, and the first
 phase of the Dandara project, comprising 569 MW solar + 100 MWh BESS
* Signed a renewable energy investment platform with EBRD, securing a
 commitment of up to USD 221 million for projects in Egypt
* Remaining D&C contract value increased by NOK 6.7 billion to NOK 10.5
 billion
* Secured equity bridge loans of USD 150 million for Energy Valley and Shadwan
* Successfully placed a NOK 1.5 billion bond at 3m NIBOR + 250bps, refinancing
 the bond placed in 2023 at significantly improved terms
In the quarter, Scatec recognised impairments of NOK 1,150 million on a
consolidated basis and NOK 1,066 million on a proportionate basis, related to
its assets in Ukraine and Pakistan. The impairments reflect increased cash
flow uncertainties, country risk premiums and long-term interest rates.
Third quarter consolidated revenues and other income were NOK 1,677 million
(1,080 million), EBITDA was NOK 1,135 million (785 million), and net profit
was NOK -1,135 million (5 million).
Outlook
* FY'26 power production 4.95-5.15 TWh
* FY'26 proportionate power production EBITDA reduced by NOK 300 million to
 NOK 3,300-3,600 million, of which NOK 80 million relates to the suspended
 reserves market in the Philippines
* Remaining D&C contract value of NOK 10.5 billion for projects under
 construction
* Estimated gross margin for projects under construction between 10% and 12%
Strategic roadmap towards 2030
Scatec's self-funded growth strategy is yielding tangible results, with good
progress on growth, deleveraging, and capital discipline over the past two
years. Building on this momentum, the company is refining its roadmap with
increased targets for the strategic period 2027-2030:
* Double average annual equity investment target to NOK 2 billion
* Double annual cash flow to equity from 2030 to more than NOK 2.5 billion
* Reduce corporate interest-bearing debt to NOK 4 billion
* Realise at least NOK 3.4 billion from divestment of assets and farm-downs
* Maintain self-funding through operating cash flow, robust D&C contribution,
 divestment proceeds, and available liquidity
* Focus on solar PV, BESS and onshore wind, both stand-alone and hybrid
 solutions
"Scatec is entering its next growth phase with a record-high portfolio that
provides strong, visible near-term growth. Our integrated business model
continues to create value across development, construction, ownership, and
operations. As energy markets evolve, we will remain focused on disciplined
execution and selective growth in the markets where our capabilities,
relationships and business model give us a clear competitive advantage. We
enter the final quarter of the year with strong momentum and a clear strategic
direction," says Scatec CEO Terje Pilskog. 
Additional information
Proportionate historical financial information on a country-by-country level
and a portfolio overview is published on the website. See definitions of the
Alternative Performance Measures in the appendix in the quarterly report.
A presentation of the third quarter results followed by a Q&A session will be
held at Scatec's headquarters at Skøyen Atrium III (1st floor), Askekroken 11,
0277 Oslo, today at 09:00 am CET. You can also follow the presentation and Q&A
session through this link: Scatec webcast Q3 2026
(https://qcnl.tv/p/1jx0Q2s8TNxUOdYU0kASPg)
For further information, please contact:
For analysts and investors:
Andreas Austrell, SVP Investor Relations
andreas.austrell@scatec.com

Meera Bhatia, SVP External Affairs & Communications
meera.bhatia@scatec.com
About Scatec
Scatec is a leading renewable energy solutions provider, accelerating access
to reliable and affordable clean energy in emerging markets. As a long-term
player, we develop, build, own, and operate renewable energy plants, with 8 GW
generation and 2.1 GWh storage capacity in operation and under construction
across five continents. We are committed to growing our renewable energy
portfolio, delivered by our passionate employees and partners who are driven
by a common vision of Improving our Future'. Scatec is headquartered in Oslo,
Norway and listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol SCATC'.
To learn more, visit www.scatec.com or connect with us on LinkedIn.

title: Good profitability and capacity for further growth
body:
SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge reports a profit before tax of NOK 2,996 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with NOK 3,296 million in the same period last year. Return on equity is 16.0 per cent, well above the Group's long-term target of 14 per cent. 
- We are delivering a good ROE and have a solid foundation for further profitable growth. Our priorities remain firm: we aim to be the first choice for people and businesses in the north, make full use of the ecosystems within the Group and the SpareBank 1 Alliance, and operate ever more efficiently, says CEO Hanne Karoline Kræmer. 
The cost-to-income ratio is 33.1 per cent, well within the Group's long-term target of below 35 per cent. 
- We launched an efficiency project in spring 2025 with the ambition of reducing annual costs by approximately NOK 50 million by the end of 2026, all else being equal. The work has been based on natural attrition, simpler work processes and cutting activities that do not create value. We have achieved this goal a few months ahead of schedule and have reduced staffing by more than 50 full-time equivalents without using severance packages or other incentives. I am pleased with that, says Kræmer, while emphasizing that the efficiency work will continue in order to maintain the Group's position as a cost leader.
Net loan losses total NOK 101 million so far this year, compared with NOK 23 million in the same period last year. The Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio is 17.0 per cent, compared with 16.2 per cent a year earlier. 
- Loss provisions are somewhat higher than at the same time last year, but most of this consists of model-based provisions. Underlying losses remain low, although we have seen a slight increase so far this year. Northern Norway is doing well, even though our region is also affected by uncertainty and geopolitical unrest. Our strong capital position and good profitability provide a sound basis for financing our customers' investments and further developing the Group's position in Northern Norway, regardless of the macroeconomic environment, says Kræmer. 
SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge presents its Q3 2026 results on Friday 30 October at 09:30 CET. Group CEO Hanne Karoline Kræmer and CFO Bengt Olsen will host the presentation in Norwegian. Watch the livestream at snn.no/investor and submit questions to investor@snn.no.
Key figures as of 30 September 2026: 
- Profit before tax: NOK 2,996 million (3,296) 
- ROE: 16 % (19 %) 
- C/I: 33.1 % (31.5 %) 
- Loan losses: NOK 101 million (23) 
- CET1 capital ratio: 17 % (16.2 %) 
(Corresponding figures for 2025 in brackets)

title: God lønnsomhet og kapasitet til videre vekst
body:
SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge leverer et resultat før skatt på 2 996 millioner kroner etter tredje kvartal 2026, mot 3 296 millioner kroner i samme periode i fjor. Egenkapitalavkastningen er 16,0 prosent, godt over konsernets langsiktige mål på 14 prosent. 
- Vi leverer god avkastning og har et solid utgangspunkt for videre lønnsom vekst. Prioriteringene våre ligger fast: Vi skal være førstevalget for folk og næringsliv i nord, utnytte bredden i konsernet og SpareBank 1-alliansen og drive stadig mer effektivt, sier konsernsjef Hanne Karoline Kræmer. 
Kostnadsprosenten er 33,1 prosent, noe som er godt innenfor konsernets langsiktige mål på under 35 prosent.
- Vi startet et effektiviseringsprogram våren 2025, med ambisjon om å redusere det årlige kostnadsnivået med om lag 50 millioner kroner innen utgangen av 2026, alt annet likt. Arbeidet har basert seg på naturlig avgang, enklere arbeidsprosesser og reduksjon av aktiviteter som ikke skaper verdi. Vi har nådd denne målsettingen, noen måneder før tiden, og har tatt ned mer enn 50 årsverk uten å bruke pakker eller andre incentiver. Det er jeg svært fornøyd med, sier Kræmer, som samtidig understreker at effektiviseringsprosessen fortsetter, for å beholde posisjonen som kostnadsledende. 
Netto utlånstap utgjør 101 millioner kroner hittil i år, mot 23 millioner kroner i samme periode i fjor. Ren kjernekapitaldekning er 17,0 prosent, mot 16,2 prosent året før. 
- Tapsavsetningene er noe høyere enn i fjor på samme tid, men det meste av dette er modellbaserte avsetninger. De underliggende tapene er fortsatt lave, selv om vi ser en liten økning hittil i år. Nord-Norge går godt, selv om også vår landsdel preges av usikkerhet og geopolitiske uroligheter. Vår sterke soliditet og gode lønnsomhet gir et godt utgangspunkt for å finansiere kundenes investeringer og videreutvikle konsernets posisjon i Nord-Norge, uansett makrokonteksten, sier Kræmer. 
SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge presenterer resultatene for tredje kvartal 2026 fredag 30. oktober kl. 09.30. Konsernsjef Hanne Karoline Kræmer og CFO Bengt Olsen presenterer resultatene. Følg direktesendingen på snn.no/investor, og send spørsmål til investor@snn.no.
Nøkkeltall per 30.9.2026: 
- Resultat før skatt: 2 996 mill. kr. (3 296) 
- EK-avkastning: 16 % (19 %) 
- Kostnadsprosent: 33,1 % (31,5 %) 
- Utlånstap: 101 mill. kr. (23) 
- Ren kjernekapitaldekning: 17 % (16,2 %)
